sections.heading: What £5.40 a month buys a tradesman
sections.html:
The advertised entry price is for public liability alone, and the site is unusually open about what real customers pay. Ten per cent of them paid £64.78 a year or less in the first half of 2026. Two worked examples are published with the date they were generated, 12 May 2026: a Manchester domestic cleaner with under a year's experience, no employees and £1,000,000 of public liability at £7.21 a month or £86.49 a year, underwritten by Covéa; and an Edinburgh barber renting a chair, with £1,000,000 of liability and £1,000 of tools cover, at £11.46 a month or £100.08 a year, underwritten by Chiswell. A separate builder's example on the trades page comes out at £7.32 a month, £87.89 for the year.

Four public liability limits are offered — £1m, £2m, £5m and £10m — and the split between them is published too: 85% of customers take £1,000,000 and 15% take £2,000,000. That figure is worth sitting with. The £1m limit is the cheapest box on the form and the one most people tick, but plenty of commercial clients, main contractors and accreditation schemes ask for more before they will let anyone on site, and the quote journey does not know what your customers demand. Employers' liability is the exception: it is set at £10,000,000 on both published wordings, which is double the £5,000,000 the law asks for.

Beyond liability, the trades journey will add tools and equipment, owned and hired plant, contract works, stock, business legal protection and personal accident. Cover can be bought the same day, with documents issued immediately.

sections.heading: Nineteen insurers on the panel, and three of them are the house
sections.html:
Simply Business publishes its panel, which is more than most brokers do. On the business side it lists AXA (with Select and Commercial Guard variants), QBE and QBE Essentials, Covéa with its Lexicon and Elements products, AIG and AIG Essentials, Allianz, Zurich, Hiscox, Markel, Churchill, and a Barclays-badged product — 19 named entries in all. Three of those entries are described on the same page as MGAs: Finsbury, Maltings and Chiswell.

Chiswell is the interesting one. It was established in 2016, it is available only through Simply Business, and its policies are underwritten by HDI Global Specialty SE and Great Lakes Insurance SE, the Munich Re subsidiary. Finsbury is presented in the same way, and Xbridge's own complaints page names Chiswell Insurance Services and Finsbury Insurance Group as associated brands. So when the barber in the published example was quoted at £11.46 a month, the quote came from the broker's own underwriting agency rather than from a third party on the panel. Nothing about that is improper — a managing general agent binds cover on a real insurer's behalf, and HDI Global Specialty and Great Lakes are substantial names — but a shopper who believes they are comparing 19 independent insurers is not quite getting that. The public liability page describes the exercise as comparing quotes from "up to 15 insurers", which is a fourth number again.

sections.heading: The wording you get is decided during the quote, not before it
sections.html:
Because the insurer is chosen by the quote engine, a tradesman cannot read the policy that will govern their claim until they have been matched to one. Two of the wordings are on open URLs, and they differ in ways that matter.

The AXA tradesmen summary (reference ACLD0784Z-A, dated 04/21) sets public liability at £1,000,000 as standard with an upgrade to a maximum of £5,000,000 — not the £10,000,000 AXA advertises on its own site. Employers' liability runs to £10,000,000 any one event. The public liability excess is £250, rising to £500 or £1,000 for certain trades. Portable tools are limited to £500 for any one item, with an excess of 10% of each claim, minimum £100 and maximum £500. Hired plant and contract works both carry a £250 excess that becomes £500 for theft. Contract works are capped at £500,000 for any one contract, stock in trade at £2,500 and constructional plant at £25,000. Personal accident pays £2,000 on death or permanent disability and up to £500 a week for 104 weeks of temporary disability. Exclusions include asbestos, defective workmanship, and work at aircraft installations, railways, docks, quarries and power stations.

The Covéa Small Business Plus wording (reference P187E, dossier 20110324E) carries the same £10,000,000 employers' liability figure, limits tools to £500 per tool or 20% of the sum insured whichever is greater, and imposes conditions precedent that a working tradesman would want to read before a claim rather than after — hot work and welding require named fire precautions, flammable solvents require further ones, and underground services must be located before digging starts. That document is dated May 2019, which is over seven years old at the time of writing. The site's own construction page puts the range of excesses across the panel at anything from nil to £750 on public liability and up to £4,000 on contents and stock, depending on which insurer you land with.

sections.heading: Taking on a first employee changes the paperwork permanently
sections.html:
Employers' liability cover is compulsory from the day a tradesman takes on staff, and Simply Business flags the fine of up to £2,500 for every day without it. The part nobody explains is what happens to the record afterwards. Since the rules in the regulator's policy statement PS11/4 of February 2011, which came into force on 6 March 2011, every insurer must maintain an employers' liability register of policies entered into, renewed or claimed on from 1 April 2011, and from 1 April 2012 must record the Employer Reference Number — the PAYE reference issued by HMRC — against each one. Directors have had to certify those registers annually, with an assurance report, since 1 July 2012. The regulator costed the set-up of the system at about £28.4 million.

The practical effect is that the ERN a tradesman gives at quote time is the thread that lets a former employee find the right insurer twenty years later, for a disease claim that may not surface until long after the business has closed. Give a wrong or missing reference and the policy is harder to trace. It takes ten seconds at the quote stage and no comparison journey makes any fuss about it.

sections.heading: Spreading the cost over twelve months
sections.html:
Monthly payments are run through a credit agreement with Premium Credit Limited rather than by Simply Business itself, and interest is charged. The rate is not published anywhere on the site: the help pages say only that "details of the interest will be shown before going ahead and included in your credit agreement, sent after purchase". The agreement has to be signed and returned electronically within ten days of receipt, and failing to do that attracts a one-off £25 penalty charge. Renewal payments are taken nine days before the current policy expires.

The two published example quotes tell slightly different stories about what the instalments cost. The cleaner's £7.21 a month multiplies out to £86.52 against an annual price of £86.49 — effectively no uplift. The barber's £11.46 a month multiplies out to £137.52 against an annual price of £100.08, which is £37.44 or roughly 37% more for paying in twelve pieces. Both are the provider's own figures, published side by side on the same page and generated on the same day.

For context, the regulator's premium finance market study MS24/2, published in February 2026, found weighted average APRs at the end of that period of 16.5% where the insurer lends, 23.5% at intermediary lenders and 29.4% at intermediary brokers — the last of those down from 35.1% in 2022. It also found that broker compensation accounted for 55% of the total cost of credit on agreements financed by specialist providers, and that commission averaged about £45 per policy and 8% of loan value in 2023. Falling rates have saved customers around £157 million a year across the market. That work looked at motor and home policies, so none of the numbers are Simply Business's, but they are the yardstick for what an insurance instalment plan usually costs, and they explain why the annual price is worth asking for.

sections.heading: The complaints numbers Simply Business publishes about itself
sections.html:
Xbridge puts its own regulatory complaints return on the website, which very few brokers do. For the six months to 31 December 2025 it opened 1,240 general insurance complaints and closed 1,319, a rate of 1.86 complaints for every 1,000 policies sold. Eleven per cent were closed within three days and 88% within eight weeks, and 40% were upheld. The preceding half year, to 30 June 2025, ran at 1,186 opened and 1,216 closed, 1.75 per 1,000 policies, 16% closed within three days, 84% within eight weeks and 46% upheld. Credit broking is reported separately and is small: 45 complaints opened in the second half of 2025 with 38% upheld, and 59 in the first half with 30% upheld.

Two things stand out. The uphold rate sits well above the 30% average the Financial Ombudsman Service records across all financial products, and only about one complaint in nine is settled inside three days. Against that, the volume is modest for a book of more than a million policies, and the firm is publishing figures it is under no obligation to make this easy to find. The rules are changing here too: the regulator's policy statement PS25/19, published in December 2025, merges five separate complaints returns into one, moves everybody to half-yearly calendar reporting and sets a publication threshold of 500 complaints or more, with the first return under the new regime covering January to June 2027.

Claims are a third party again. Simply Business states that "our specialist partner Sedgwick pays claims on behalf of the insurer", on 0333 207 0560 around the clock, with a call back within two days of an online form and payment usually within 24 hours of a settlement being agreed. So a tradesman who buys here deals with the broker at the quote, an insurer or MGA on the certificate, a loss adjuster at the claim and a separate lender if paying monthly.

sections.heading: Where the paperwork runs out
sections.html:
The one document a broker's customer most wants before buying is the terms of business agreement, because that is where set-up fees, mid-term adjustment charges and cancellation fees live. Simply Business does not publish it. Its help pages point to it repeatedly — cancelling after the 14-day cooling-off period gives "a proportionate refund of the premium you have paid, less any set up fees and the cancellation fee as set out in your Terms of Business Agreement" — and the website terms, dated June 2026, confirm the TOBA exists and governs the relationship without saying what is in it. Searching the site turns up no copy. The one piece of good news is explicit: "there is no admin fee to make a change to your policy."

Independent ratings are thin, and partly that is the market rather than the firm. Defaqto rates insurance products rather than the brokers who introduce them, and commercial cover is much less thoroughly rated than home or motor, so no star rating for this product could be found. Smart Money People carries a business insurance score of 4.61 out of 5 from 32 reviews, last reviewed on 20 August 2026, plus 4.27 from 8 reviews on liability and 4.14 from 44 on landlord cover — small samples, and worth treating as such. The 4.5 out of 5 from about 40,000 reviews shown across the site is collected by Feefo on the firm's own behalf and carries no date or product breakdown.

Xbridge files full accounts at Companies House, most recently made up to 31 December 2025 and filed on 15 July 2026, so its revenue and commission income are a matter of public record for anyone who wants to order the document; the filing itself could not be read for this review. The firm reference, 313348, is verifiable on the Financial Services Register.

pros: Genuine breadth for a one-person business: 19 named insurers and MGAs including AXA, Aviva, Zurich, Allianz, QBE, Covéa, Hiscox and Markel
Prices published with real dated examples rather than vague 'from' claims — £7.21 a month for a cleaner, £11.46 for a barber, both quoted 12 May 2026
Employers' liability at £10,000,000 on the published wordings, double the £5,000,000 legal minimum
No administration fee for mid-term changes, which many brokers charge £25 to £50 for
Publishes its own complaints return openly, including the uphold rate, which most brokers bury
£57 million of claims paid in 2025 and settlement payments usually made within 24 hours of agreement
Owned by Travelers since 2017, so the broker sits behind a large balance sheet
cons: The terms of business agreement is not published, so set-up and cancellation fees cannot be seen before buying — only the 'no admin fee' for changes is stated openly

Three of the panel entries — Chiswell, Finsbury and Maltings — are managing general agents rather than independent insurers, and Chiswell is available only through Simply Business, so a 'comparison' can return the house's own product
The panel is described as 19 named entries on one page and 'up to 15 insurers' on another
40% of complaints were upheld in the six months to 31 December 2025, against a 30% average across all financial products, and only 11% were closed within three days
The interest rate for paying monthly is not disclosed until checkout, and the barber example on the site works out 37% more expensive paid monthly than paid annually
A £25 penalty applies if the Premium Credit agreement is not signed and returned within ten days
The Covéa Small Business Plus wording on open display is dated May 2019, and the AXA tradesmen summary 04/21
Public liability through this route tops out at £5,000,000 on the AXA product, where AXA sells £10,000,000 direct
No Defaqto rating for the product, and the independent review samples that do exist are small (32 reviews on business insurance)
The service is non-advised, so nobody checks whether the £1,000,000 limit 85% of customers pick is enough for the contracts they work on
verdict: For a self-employed tradesman who wants liability cover quickly and cheaply, Simply Business does the job it advertises: real insurers, real prices, a quote in minutes and no charge for changing the policy later. The published claims and complaints figures are more than most brokers will show you, and the Travelers ownership means the business behind the website is not going anywhere. The reservations are about what happens after the quote. You cannot see the fee schedule before you buy, you cannot see the interest rate on instalments before you buy, and you cannot read the wording that will govern your claim until the engine has picked your insurer. None of that is unusual in this corner of the market, but it does mean the cheapest quote on the screen is not necessarily the cheapest policy over a year. Ask for the annual price, ask which insurer you have been placed with, and check the public liability limit against what your customers actually require before you tick the £1,000,000 box.

faqs.q: Does Simply Business insure me itself?
faqs.a: No. Simply Business is the trading name of Xbridge Limited, an insurance broker with FCA firm reference 313348. It arranges the policy and the risk is carried by one of the insurers or managing general agents on its panel, such as AXA, Covéa, Zurich, QBE or its own Chiswell agency, whose policies are underwritten by HDI Global Specialty SE and Great Lakes Insurance SE.

faqs.q: How much public liability cover do I actually need?
faqs.a: There is no legal minimum. Simply Business offers £1m, £2m, £5m and £10m, and 85% of its customers take £1,000,000. The limit that matters is whichever your clients, your accreditation scheme or your contract requires, which can be higher — so check before you pick the cheapest option, because the quote form will not ask.

faqs.q: What does it cost to cancel?
faqs.a: Within the first 14 days you are charged only for the time on cover. After that you get a proportionate refund less any set-up fees and a cancellation fee. Neither figure is published on the website; both are set out in the terms of business agreement issued with your policy, so ask for the amounts before you buy.

faqs.q: Is paying monthly more expensive?
faqs.a: Yes, interest is charged, through a credit agreement with Premium Credit Limited rather than with Simply Business. The rate is only shown at checkout. On the firm's own published examples, one quote works out at the same price either way while another costs £137.52 a year monthly against £100.08 paid up front. There is also a £25 charge if the credit agreement is not signed and returned within ten days.

faqs.q: Who handles a claim?
faqs.a: Sedgwick, which the site describes as paying claims on behalf of the insurer, on 0333 207 0560 at any hour. An online form gets a call back within two days, and once a settlement is agreed payment is usually made by bank transfer within 24 hours. Simply Business paid out £57 million in 2025, an average of about £156,000 a day.

faqs.q: Do I need to give my PAYE reference?
faqs.a: If you employ anyone, yes. Insurers must record the Employer Reference Number against every employers' liability policy renewed since 1 April 2012 and keep it on a register that a former employee can search years later. Getting it right at the quote stage is what allows an old claim to find the right insurer once the business has gone.

title: Smart Cover Plumbing and Drainage Insurance
meta_title: Smart Cover Plumbing & Drainage: £6.27 a Month Explained
meta_description: Smart Cover's plumbing and drainage plan starts at £6.27 a month. The claim limits, excesses, waiting periods and small print, checked at source.
intro:
Smart Cover has been selling household emergency policies since Smart-Cover Direct Limited was incorporated on 18 April 2013, and the plumbing and drainage plan is the cheapest thing it sells for the home: £6.27 a month, discounted from £6.96. That buys a 24-hour claims line, an approved engineer sent out within 24 hours of a claim being approved, and the callout, labour and parts included rather than billed separately. For a single blocked drain or a burst internal pipe, one claim can cost more than a year of premiums.

The range around it is broad for a firm this size. Plumbing and drainage on its own is £6.27; adding internal electrical emergencies takes it to £9.00 a month; the Smart Home Essential plan, which folds in the boiler, the central heating system and the external water supply pipe, is £10.90. Boiler-only cover starts at £7.90 and the top Smart Home Plus plan, which adds lock and key assistance and pest infestation, is £12.90. Every plan lets you pick an excess of £0, £49, £69 or £99, which is more choice than most home emergency products give you.

The claims line is 03333 449 559, staffed around the clock, and Smart Cover says calls are typically answered inside 60 seconds. There is a separate plumbing claims number, 03333 449 247. Complaints are acknowledged within five business days and answered inside the eight weeks the FCA allows, after which the Financial Ombudsman Service will take the case.

sections.heading: What the £6.27 plan covers, and where the ceilings sit
sections.html:
The base plan handles an internal plumbing emergency, an internal drainage emergency, and a blockage or leak in the external water supply pipe running from your boundary to the house. Add electrics and the plan carries a £1,000 annual limit with £250 payable on any single claim. Step up to Smart Home Essential at £10.90 and the annual limit becomes unlimited while the per-claim ceiling rises to £500, with a £99 excess attached.

Those two numbers are the ones worth writing down. An annual cap of £1,000 is generous against a £75.24 yearly premium, but the £250 per-claim ceiling on the mid plan is the real constraint — it is the figure that decides whether a job is covered outright or part-paid. The Financial Ombudsman Service, describing the boiler settlements it sees in home emergency disputes, puts typical figures at around £250 to £500, which places the mid plan's ceiling at the bottom of that range and Smart Home Essential's at the top.

Excess choice cuts both ways. Taking the £0 excess on the plumbing plan means a small blocked-drain job costs you nothing beyond the premium; taking £49 or £99 lowers the monthly price but can wipe out the value of a modest claim entirely. On a £250 per-claim ceiling, a £99 excess leaves £151 of usable cover.

sections.heading: Who sells this policy and who stands behind it
sections.html:
Smart Cover is a trading name of Smart-Cover Direct Limited, company number 08493961, registered at Ashley Court, 32 Main Street, Ashley, Leicestershire LE16 8HF and operating from Citibase, 42–44 Clarendon Road, Watford WD17 1JJ. It holds FCA reference number 600428 and is an Appointed Representative of City and Commercial Limited, FRN 314346. Both numbers are checkable on the FCA Register. Companies House records the firm under SIC code 66220, the code for insurance agents and brokers, and its last accounts were made up to 31 May 2025.

An Appointed Representative does not hold its own FCA permissions. It trades under the authorisation of a principal firm, which is answerable for what it does. The arrangement is common and entirely legitimate — the FCA counts thousands of them — but the regulator has been blunt about the record. Announcing tighter rules on 3 August 2022, it said principals generate up to 400 per cent more supervisory cases and complaints than comparable directly authorised firms, and that principals and their representatives together account for more than 60 per cent of the value of recent claims on the Financial Services Compensation Scheme. That is a statement about a whole regime rather than about this firm, and it is a reason to read the paperwork rather than a reason to walk away.

One point could not be settled from public sources. Smart Cover's own pages describe City and Commercial Limited as the underwriter, but City and Commercial is an authorised intermediary and Smart-Cover Direct's principal, which is a different job from carrying insurance risk. The insurer actually standing behind the plumbing policy is not named anywhere on the public site, and that needs confirming with Smart Cover before you buy.

sections.heading: How this sits alongside cover you may already hold
sections.html:
Two things already sit in the same space. The first is your buildings insurance, which pays for the damage an escape of water does — the sodden floor, the ruined ceiling — while a home emergency policy stops the leak. The Ombudsman spells the split out plainly: home emergency policies "don't usually cover any damage the emergency has caused" and often deliver a temporary fix rather than a permanent one. The two products are complements, not substitutes, and neither replaces the other. Association of British Insurers figures published on 19 February 2026 put total property claims for 2025 at £6.1 billion with the average home claim at £6,000, up 15 per cent year on year, against average combined buildings and contents premiums of £379 in the fourth quarter of 2025.

The second is your water company. The external supply pipe that the plan covers is your responsibility in law once it passes the outside stop tap, and the water companies enforce that. Severn Trent starts its Defective Water Fittings enforcement process if a confirmed leak on a private supply pipe is not repaired within 14 days, and offers a metered customer a single leakage allowance towards the water lost, claimable once, provided the repair is done inside those 14 days. Thames Water gives four weeks to arrange a repair. Some suppliers go further and will repair a customer's supply pipe free once — worth a phone call to your own water company before you pay a monthly premium for the same thing.

sections.heading: The conditions that decide whether a claim is paid
sections.html:
New policies do not pay straight away. A homeowner cannot claim within 14 days of the start date and a landlord cannot claim within 28 days. Boiler service cover carries a 30-day wait and appliance cover 45 days, stretching to six months on some items. Buying on the day a drain blocks will not help.

The exclusions are the standard shape for the product and are stated openly: general maintenance, pre-existing damage or faults, anything that is not sudden and unforeseen, the removal of limescale, sludge or debris, and any fault whose origin is traced outside the property. Boilers not serviced in the previous 12 months fall outside cover, and a fault that only costs you hot water rather than heating may not count as an emergency at all.

Cancellation terms are worth reading before you commit. Inside the 14-day cooling-off period you get a full refund provided you have not claimed. After that, an annual policy is refunded pro rata for the unused months less a £15 administration fee, while monthly and quarterly policies typically get nothing back. Refunds land in three to five business days. Smart Cover also runs a price match against identical policies from other FCA-authorised firms, though it excludes competitor offers discounted by more than 20 per cent.

sections.heading: What the regulator's own numbers say about this product line
sections.html:
Home emergency cover is one of the few products the FCA singled out for value measurement. Its pilot data for the year ending 31 August 2019, published on 8 September 2020, drew returns from 16 firms and found claims frequency ranging from 2.5 per cent to 92.4 per cent, claims acceptance from 80 per cent to 100 per cent, and average payouts from £90 to £270. The spread is the point: some books saw almost every policyholder claim, others almost none, and the average settlement across all of them sat below or barely above one year's premium on a plan like this.

Set £270 — the top of that payout range — against £75.24 a year for the plumbing plan and the arithmetic is reasonable if you claim roughly once every three or four years. Set £90, the bottom of the range, against the same premium and the policy is buying convenience and a 24-hour number rather than saving money. Which of those two you are buying depends almost entirely on the age and state of your pipework, and it is a calculation worth doing honestly before you sign up.

Home emergency was not carried in the FCA's most recent general insurance value measures release of 21 July 2026, which covers home, motor, travel and pet, so there is no current acceptance-rate figure for the line and none for Smart Cover specifically. Independently, Smart Money People rates the firm 4.46 out of 5 across 83 reviews, with home emergency cover at 4.65 from 33 reviews and appliance insurance at 4.20 from 50. Those are small samples and should be read as such. No Defaqto star rating for this product could be found.

sections.heading: Where these policies most often go wrong
sections.html:
The Ombudsman publishes the pattern of disputes it sees on home emergency cover, and it is a useful checklist for anyone about to buy one. The recurring complaints are claims turned down because the insurer did not accept the incident was an emergency, delayed or cancelled engineer appointments, temporary repairs left in place of permanent ones, damage caused during a repair, the wrong excess charged, and mis-selling. Six published case studies cover those grounds.

Two of Smart Cover's own rules feed directly into that list. All work must be done by its approved, Gas Safe registered engineers, and the firm states plainly that costs for independently arranged repairs cannot be reimbursed. If you cannot wait and call a local plumber yourself at two in the morning, you pay twice. And because a claim must be approved before an engineer is dispatched, the definition of an emergency is decided by the insurer at the point you most need a decision.

The gap that matters most is the documentation. A policy wording or Insurance Product Information Document for the plumbing and drainage plan could not be found published anywhere on the public site; the pages summarise cover and the claims process points customers to the policy schedule or IPID they receive after buying. Ask for the full wording and the schedule before you pay, not after, and read what it says about per-claim limits and the definition of an emergency.

pros: £6.27 a month is genuinely cheap for internal plumbing and drainage cover with callout, labour and parts included
A choice of £0, £49, £69 or £99 excess is more flexibility than most home emergency products offer
Unlimited annual claim limit on the Smart Home Essential plan, with a £500 per-claim ceiling
24-hour claims line answered in around 60 seconds, engineer within 24 hours of approval
External water supply pipe leaks and blockages are included, which some cheaper plans leave out
Regulatory position is disclosed openly, with both firm reference numbers published on the site
cons: No policy wording or Insurance Product Information Document appears to be published before purchase, so you cannot read the full terms until after you have paid
The insurer carrying the risk is not named publicly; the site describes its principal firm, an authorised intermediary, as the underwriter, which needs confirming
You cannot use your own plumber — independently arranged repairs are not reimbursed, however long you wait for an approved engineer
A £250 per-claim limit on the £9.00 plan sits at the bottom of the £250 to £500 range the Ombudsman cites for typical home emergency settlements
Monthly and quarterly policies typically get no refund on cancellation, and annual ones carry a £15 administration fee
External supply pipe cover may duplicate what your water company will already do, and the policy does not pay for water damage your buildings insurer handles
verdict: As a low-cost way to have a 24-hour number and a plumber who arrives without a bill, Smart Cover's £6.27 plan does what it says, and the excess choice is better than most. The catch is that you are buying it partly blind: the full wording is not published in advance and the insurer behind it is not named, so ask for both before you pay. Worth it if your pipework is old and you would rather not hunt for an emergency plumber at midnight; harder to justify if your water company already fixes supply pipes free and your buildings policy is doing the heavy lifting anyway.

faqs.q: How soon can I claim after taking out the policy?
faqs.a: A homeowner has to wait 14 days from the start date and a landlord 28 days. Boiler service cover carries a 30-day wait and appliance cover 45 days, extending to six months on some items. Nothing that goes wrong inside those windows is covered.

faqs.q: Does the plumbing plan pay for the damage a leak causes?
faqs.a: No. Home emergency cover stops the emergency; the damage is a buildings and contents insurance claim. The Financial Ombudsman Service makes this point explicitly, noting these policies do not usually cover damage the emergency has caused and sometimes provide a temporary rather than a permanent repair.

faqs.q: Can I call out my own plumber and claim the cost back?
faqs.a: No. All work must be carried out by Smart Cover's approved, Gas Safe registered engineers, and the firm states that costs for independently arranged repairs cannot be reimbursed. An engineer is dispatched within 24 hours of a claim being approved.

faqs.q: What does it cost to cancel?
faqs.a: Within 14 days of buying you get a full refund provided no claim has been made. After that, an annual policy is refunded pro rata for the unused months less a £15 administration fee, and monthly or quarterly policies typically receive nothing back. Refunds are processed in three to five business days.

faqs.q: Who regulates Smart Cover?
faqs.a: Smart-Cover Direct Limited holds FCA reference number 600428 and trades as an Appointed Representative of City and Commercial Limited, FRN 314346, which holds the FCA authorisation. Both are searchable on the FCA Register. Complaints go to Smart Cover first, on 03333 449 559, and to the Financial Ombudsman Service on 0800 023 4567 if unresolved after eight weeks.

faqs.q: Is the external water supply pipe worth insuring separately?
faqs.a: Check with your water company first. The pipe from your boundary to the house is legally yours to maintain, and suppliers enforce that — Severn Trent begins its Defective Water Fittings process if a confirmed leak is not repaired within 14 days, Thames Water allows four weeks — but several suppliers will repair a customer supply pipe free of charge, and Severn Trent offers metered customers a one-off leakage allowance for the water lost if the repair is done inside 14 days.

title: Start Rescue Breakdown Cover Review
meta_title: Start Rescue Review: Which?-Rated Cover From £31.58 a Year
meta_description: Start Rescue's five tiers from £31.58, a 78% roadside fix rate and a 10-mile local recovery limit. What the policy document says before you buy.
intro:
Start Rescue is the retail brand of Call Assist Limited, a Colchester company incorporated on 16 November 1998 and still run from Axis Court on North Station Road. It is not a patrol force in the mould of the AA or the RAC. Call Assist buys recovery capacity from a network of more than 400 approved recovery operators across the UK and a further network reaching over 45 countries in Europe, and sells the cover under its own name. Group-wide it says it looks after over 2 million breakdown customers.

The pricing is the reason most people arrive. One Star vehicle cover starts at £31.58 a year or £3.16 a month, and the most popular Three Star policy — roadside, nationwide recovery and home assistance — is £55.12 a year. Start Rescue's own renewal page sets that against rival three-star equivalents priced between £70.85 and £172.06. Add a second vehicle and a further 10% comes off.

Cheap breakdown cover has a reputation, and this is the part that separates Start Rescue from it: the company has been a Which? Recommended Provider every year since 2019, taking a seventh consecutive title in 2025 on an 86% customer score, and its Three Star policy carries a Defaqto 5 Star expert rating. Its own service data for November 2025 to April 2026 puts over 78% of vehicles repaired at the roadside, against a target of a recovery operator with you inside 60 minutes.

sections.heading: The five-rung ladder, and where the money goes
sections.html:
Cover is sold in stars rather than named tiers, and each rung buys one clearly defined thing.

One Star, £31.58 a year, is roadside assistance plus local recovery within 10 miles. That radius is the whole product: break down 12 miles from home and the recovery operator has no obligation to take you the rest of the way. Two Star, £46.76, replaces the 10-mile limit with nationwide recovery, which for most drivers is the single most useful upgrade on the page. Three Star, £55.12, adds home assistance. Four Star, £90.37, adds European cover and a theft and break-in benefit. Five Star, £106.66, adds accident, theft and vandalism cover plus assistance where the driver is taken ill or injured, worth up to £1,000.

Monthly payment is offered at £3.16, £4.68 and £5.51 for the bottom three rungs. Four and Five Star are annual-payment only. Personal cover, which follows the driver into any eligible vehicle rather than sitting on one registration, is also restricted to the first three tiers.

The benefit limits are identical across the ladder and are worth knowing before you need them: up to £250 towards alternative transport or a hire vehicle up to 1600cc, up to £150 for one person to travel back and collect the repaired car, and emergency accommodation at £150 for a lone traveller or £75 each, capped at £500 per incident. Misfuelling assistance is also capped at £250. Abroad, the accommodation cap rises to £1,000 per incident and alternative travel to £500, with £200 for two people to return for the vehicle and a £200 reimbursement ceiling on private towing off a European motorway.

sections.heading: The product the regulator does not score
sections.html:
Anyone comparing car or home insurance has two public yardsticks. Neither exists here, and that is worth understanding before you weigh any breakdown provider against another.

The FCA published its general insurance value measures data for 2025 on 21 July 2026. It reports claims acceptance rates, claims complaints and claims costs as a share of premium across dozens of retail products — motor sits at 99% acceptance, home combined at 62 to 71%, travel at 83 to 86%. Breakdown is absent, and deliberately so: the FCA states that it is not requiring firms to report claims cost information for legal expenses insurance or vehicle breakdown insurance. There is no official acceptance rate for this product line, from Start Rescue or anyone else, and any page quoting one has made it up.

The second gap is pricing. ICOBS 6B, the rulebook chapter that bans charging existing customers more than an equivalent new customer at renewal, applies only "in relation to a home insurance or motor insurance policy or any related additional product sold to a consumer". A standalone breakdown policy bought direct is neither. Start Rescue's pledge that customers "never pay more than our standard website retail prices" is therefore a commercial promise it has chosen to make, not a rule the FCA can enforce against it. That is a point in its favour — most of the market makes no such promise — but it is a promise, and the company also notes that a renewal price can still rise as the vehicle ages.

With no regulatory scorecard, the policy document is the evidence. The rest of this page works from it.

sections.heading: Who actually carries the risk
sections.html:
Call Assist Limited arranges and administers the policy under FCA firm reference 304838, which covers insurance distribution. It does not carry the risk. For policies starting on or after 1 November 2024 the insurer is ARAG Legal Expenses Insurance Company Limited, firm reference 202106, a Caerphilly-registered company originally incorporated on 28 May 1909 and authorised by the Prudential Regulation Authority. Policies that began on or before 31 October 2024 remain with Ageas Insurance Limited, firm reference 202039. If you are renewing something bought in 2023, the name on the claim is not the name on this year's certificate.

ARAG is best known in Britain as a legal expenses underwriter, which surprises people, though the arrangement is ordinary enough in the assistance market. What matters practically is that the claims decision belongs to the insurer, and the recovery itself belongs to a third contracted party — the local operator dispatched from that 400-strong network. Three organisations stand between the phone call and the tow.

Start Rescue's own agreement is explicit that the sale is non-advised: "you will not receive personalised advice or recommendations". It also states the firm "may act on behalf of the insurer" in handling your premium, so money paid to Start Rescue counts as received by the insurer, and that it "may also receive a commission and/or other economic benefits from the insurer". Choosing your own tier is your job, and the five-rung ladder is designed so that the £31.58 headline is the one you see first.

sections.heading: Limits that decide whether a claim pays
sections.html:
Read the Insurance Product Information Document and a handful of conditions do most of the work.

The first 24 hours. Any claim within 24 hours of buying is excluded. Buying cover from the hard shoulder does not work, which is the point of the rule.

The next 48. Whatever tier you paid for, "for the first 48 hours from the start date of your policy, cover is limited to One Star cover only". Pay £106.66 for Five Star on a Friday and you have 10-mile local recovery until Sunday. Mid-policy upgrades need the same 48 hours' notice.

One mile from your door. On tiers without home assistance, help "within 1 mile radius/straight line of your registered home address" is excluded. Most breakdowns happen on a cold morning on the drive, which is what makes the £8.36 step from Two Star to Three Star the one worth thinking hardest about.

Six claims, £15,000. The IPID caps cover at "maximum six (6) claims per period of insurance" and at claims "totalling more than £15,000 in any one period". A repeat of the same fault inside 28 days is excluded unless you can show the vehicle was permanently repaired and roadworthy.

Vehicle rules. Cars and motorcycles of any age qualify and vans up to 3.5 tonnes, but vans over 8 years old at inception are excluded, and for European travel the policy excludes "vehicles over 10 years old at the date this policy incepted". Towed caravans and trailers must not exceed 7 metres, or 23 feet, and must use a standard 50mm tow ball. Minibuses, limousines, motorhomes, horseboxes, campervans and anything with more than ten seats are out, as are racing, rental, hire and courier use. Cover runs across Great Britain, Northern Ireland, the Isle of Man, and Jersey and Guernsey for non-residents.

sections.heading: Where the sales page and the policy wording part company
sections.html:
The breakdown cover page lists "unlimited callouts" among the standard benefits of every tier, and the FAQ repeats it: "We allow unlimited call-outs for each vehicle that is insured". The Insurance Product Information Document for the same product restricts cover to six claims per period of insurance and £15,000 in total. Both statements come from Start Rescue. Only one of them is the contract, and it is the shorter number. Six callouts is more than most drivers will ever use and the limit is far from the meanest in the market, but a page advertising "unlimited" while its own key facts document says six is the kind of gap the Financial Ombudsman looks at closely, and it should be reconciled.

Refunds are the second place to slow down. The 14-day cooling-off period returns the premium and the arrangement and administration fee in full, provided no claim has been made. After that the wording is flat: "you will not be eligible for any refund of premium or the Fee". Pay £106.66 in January, sell the car in March, and there is nothing to reclaim. The one exception runs the other way — if Start Rescue cancels, giving seven days' written notice, and no claim has been made in the first six months, the premium and the fee are refunded in full.

The fee itself is the third. The arrangement and administration agreement confirms a fee is charged and that it "varies" with the risk, but never states an amount. The advertised £31.58 is described as including insurance premium tax and fees, so the total is what it says — you simply cannot see the split, or what the fee would be on a different vehicle, until you have run a quote.

sections.heading: Complaints, and what the Ombudsman sees
sections.html:
Complaints go to Start Rescue first. The policy terms commit to acknowledging one within five working days and responding within 20 working days. If the answer is unsatisfactory, the Financial Ombudsman Service at Exchange Tower, London E14 9SR takes it free of charge on 0800 023 4567 or 0300 123 9123, and you have six months from the final response to refer it.

The Ombudsman publishes what breakdown complaints are actually about, and the list is a fair checklist for any provider. Renewal features twice — policies renewed automatically when the customer no longer wanted them, and policies not renewed when the customer assumed they would be. Then premiums rising sharply at renewal, being charged more for a policy at the roadside, ending up with dual cover through two overlapping policies, mechanics taking too long to arrive, incorrect advice or a fault caused during a repair, and vehicles damaged during recovery. On timing, the Ombudsman says it weighs "what you advertise as your usual timeframes" — which makes Start Rescue's published 60-minute target a commitment it can be measured against, not marketing.

Start Rescue auto-renews both annual and continuous monthly policies by default, and given how often the Ombudsman sees renewal disputes, the setting is worth finding in the online account at the point of purchase rather than eleven months later. Note also that a monthly policy can only be stopped up to two days before the next period begins.

pros: Which? Recommended Provider every year since 2019, a seventh consecutive title in 2025 on an 86% customer score
Defaqto 5 Star expert rating on the Three Star policy, the tier most buyers choose
£31.58 a year entry price, and £55.12 for roadside, nationwide recovery and home assistance
Over 78% of vehicles fixed at the roadside between November 2025 and April 2026, against a 60-minute attendance target
A written pledge that renewing customers pay no more than the website retail price, which no FCA rule obliges a breakdown insurer to give
Benefit limits are identical at every tier, so the cheap policy is not quietly a weaker one on alternative travel or accommodation
10% off a second vehicle, and personal cover available on the bottom three tiers for people who drive more than one car
Underwritten by a PRA-authorised UK insurer, with premium paid to Start Rescue treated as received by that insurer
cons: The sales page and FAQ advertise "unlimited call-outs" while the Insurance Product Information Document for the same product caps cover at six claims and £15,000 per period of insurance. The contract is the smaller number
No refund whatsoever after the 14-day cooling-off period, even on an annual policy paid up front and cancelled in month two
Whatever tier you buy, cover is restricted to One Star for the first 48 hours, and nothing at all is payable in the first 24. Five Star bought on a Friday is 10-mile local recovery until Sunday
The arrangement and administration fee is confirmed in writing but its amount is never published, so the premium and the fee cannot be separated until you run a quote
Four and Five Star are annual-payment only, so the £3.16-a-month headline never applies to European or driver-illness cover
The sale is explicitly non-advised and the firm may take commission from the insurer, so picking the right rung of a five-rung ladder is entirely on the buyer
Vans over 8 years old are excluded outright, and no vehicle over 10 years old at inception is covered for European travel, despite cars "of any age" qualifying for UK cover
Underwriting moved from Ageas to ARAG on 1 November 2024, so long-standing customers are not with the insurer they originally bought from
verdict: Start Rescue does the cheap end of breakdown cover properly, which is rarer than the price suggests. Seven consecutive Which? Recommended Provider titles, a Defaqto 5 Star rating on the £55.12 Three Star policy and a 78% roadside fix rate are the numbers that matter, and the benefit limits do not shrink as the price falls. The catches are structural rather than hidden: 10-mile recovery at One Star, a one-mile exclusion around your own home below Three Star, One Star cover for the first 48 hours, and no refund at all once 14 days have passed. Two Star at £46.76 buys nationwide recovery and Three Star at £55.12 buys the driveway, and for most households that £8.36 step is the decision. The gap between an advertised "unlimited call-outs" and a policy document that says six is the one thing Start Rescue should tidy up.

faqs.q: How soon after buying am I covered?
faqs.a: Not immediately. Claims within 24 hours of purchase are excluded, and for the first 48 hours from the start date cover is limited to One Star — roadside assistance and local recovery within 10 miles — whatever tier you paid for. Upgrading an existing policy also needs 48 hours' notice before the higher cover applies.

faqs.q: Will they come out to my driveway?
faqs.a: Only on Three Star and above. One and Two Star exclude "home assistance or assistance within 1 mile radius/straight line of your registered home address". Three Star, at £55.12 a year, is £8.36 more than Two Star and is what buys that first mile.

faqs.q: Is it really unlimited callouts?
faqs.a: The website and FAQ say unlimited. The Insurance Product Information Document for the same policy says "maximum six (6) claims per period of insurance" and excludes claims totalling more than £15,000 in any one period. A repeat of the same fault within 28 days is also excluded unless the vehicle was permanently repaired. Treat six as the working figure and ask Start Rescue to confirm which document governs.

faqs.q: Who pays the claim?
faqs.a: ARAG Legal Expenses Insurance Company Limited, firm reference 202106, for policies starting on or after 1 November 2024. Policies that began on or before 31 October 2024 are still underwritten by Ageas Insurance Limited, firm reference 202039. Call Assist Limited, firm reference 304838, arranges and administers the cover but does not carry the risk. All three references are checkable on the FCA Register.

faqs.q: Can I get my money back if I cancel?
faqs.a: Within 14 days of the start date or of receiving your documents, whichever is later, you get the premium and the arrangement and administration fee back in full provided no claim has been made. After 14 days there is no refund on either an annual or a continuous monthly policy, though a monthly policy can be stopped up to two days before the next period begins.

faqs.q: What does European cover include?
faqs.a: It sits on Four Star at £90.37 and Five Star at £106.66, and the network reaches over 45 countries. Abroad the limits are up to £500 for alternative travel, £150 per person for emergency accommodation to a maximum of £1,000 per incident, £200 for two people to return and collect the vehicle, and up to £200 reimbursed for private towing off a motorway. Vehicles over 10 years old at the policy's inception date are not covered for European travel.

faqs.q: How do I complain?
faqs.a: Start Rescue acknowledges a complaint within five working days and aims to respond within 20. If you are unhappy with the answer, the Financial Ombudsman Service at Exchange Tower, London E14 9SR will look at it free of charge on 0800 023 4567 or 0300 123 9123, and you have six months from the final response to refer it.

title: AA Breakdown Cover Review
meta_title: AA Breakdown Cover Review: 2,753 Patrols, From £5.49
meta_description: The AA runs 2,753 of its own patrols and fixes 8 in 10 cars at the roadside. What the membership documents say about limits, add-ons and year two.
intro:
The AA has been going since 1905 and is, on any measure of size, the biggest breakdown operation in the country. The membership is sold by Automobile Association Insurance Services Limited from Level 3, Plant, Basing View, Basingstoke, under Financial Conduct Authority firm reference 310562. Its annual report for the year to 31 January 2026 counts 2,753 patrols on the payroll, 3.5 million breakdowns attended and 3.3 million paid personal roadside members, which the company puts at more than 40% of the consumer market.

Those patrols are the reason to pay the AA rather than a cheaper name. They are employed directly rather than subcontracted, and the AA's own service data for 1 April 2025 to 31 March 2026 has them repairing 8 in 10 cars at the roadside instead of towing them, arriving inside the hour and getting most drivers moving again in around 30 minutes. Every patrol holds the Level 1 electric vehicle awareness qualification and more than 98% hold Level 2, which matters more each year. Defaqto gives the AA a 5 Star expert rating where Roadside Assistance is bought together with National Recovery, At Home and Onward Travel.

Price is where the AA has become more competitive than its reputation suggests. Between 1 April and 30 June 2026, 10% of new customers paid £5.49 a month for vehicle-based Roadside Assistance. A 40% discount runs online until 31 August 2026 on any package that includes At Home, National Recovery or Onward Travel, applied to the first year for new customers.

sections.heading: Four blocks of cover, and the point at which each one stops
sections.html:
Roadside Assistance is the base. A patrol attends anywhere in the UK more than a quarter of a mile from the address on your membership, and call-outs are unlimited. Parts worth up to £5 are fitted free; anything dearer is charged. At Home closes the quarter-mile gap, covering the registered address and the surrounding quarter of a mile, with recovery to a nearby garage if the car cannot be fixed on the drive.

National Recovery takes the driver, the vehicle and up to seven passengers to any single destination in the UK when a roadside repair is not possible. Onward Travel deals with the rest of the day: a mid-range saloon or hatchback hire car for up to 72 hours, or one night of bed and breakfast at a hotel the AA picks, or the cost of a train, bus or coach for the driver and seven passengers to where they were going. Taxis are not paid for, and Onward Travel is limited to three claims in any one membership year.

Three add-ons sit outside the recovery service. Parts and Garage Cover pays up to £535 per claim towards parts, labour and VAT with a £35 excess, after a 14-day wait, capped at five paid claims in 12 months (six on multi-vehicle joint or family membership). Tyre Cover pays up to £160 per tyre. Key Cover is sold separately and also carries a 14-day wait. Any vehicle on the policy must be under 3.5 tonnes, no more than 2.55 metres wide and 7 metres long — petrol, diesel, electric or hydrogen, of any age, including vans, minibuses, motorhomes and motorcycles.

sections.heading: Buying it round the person instead of the car
sections.html:
The choice that changes the price most is not the tier but the basis. Vehicle cover attaches to one registration and travels with the car whoever is driving it. Personal cover attaches to you and works in any eligible vehicle, as driver or as passenger, which is the version worth paying for if you regularly drive a partner's car, a parent's car or a borrowed one.

Personal membership can be taken for one person, extended to a second on joint cover, or stretched to three further household members — all of whom must live at the same address. A hire car is covered only with the rental company's permission, and a fleet of three or more vehicles has to move to the AA's commercial product rather than sit on a personal membership.

sections.heading: Who is actually standing behind each promise
sections.html:
One membership number hides five companies. Automobile Association Insurance Services Limited, firm reference 310562, arranges everything. The recovery services themselves — Roadside, At Home and National Recovery — come from Automobile Association Developments Limited, trading as AA Breakdown Services, with AA Underwriting Insurance Company Limited providing part of the Roadside element. Onward Travel and Parts and Garage Cover are insurance policies underwritten by Acromas Insurance Company Limited, authorised by the Financial Services Commission in Gibraltar and operating from a UK branch at Enbrook Park, Sandgate, Folkestone. Tyre Cover is underwritten by Astrenska Insurance Limited, trading as Collinson Insurance.

The group behind them was taken off the London market in a buyout completed on 29 March 2021 by TowerBrook Capital Partners and Warburg Pincus, with Stonepeak joining as an investor in December 2023. The accounts for the year to 31 January 2026 show revenue of £1,505m, adjusted EBITDA of £481m and net debt of £1,906m, with average income per member reported at around £200. A debt pile close to four times earnings is not a reason to avoid the AA, but it is the commercial pressure that sits behind renewal pricing, and it is a matter of public record rather than speculation.

sections.heading: The Ombudsman cannot look at most of what you have bought
sections.html:
This is the part of AA membership least understood by the people buying it, and it is not the AA's invention — it follows from the fact that a recovery service is a service contract, not a contract of insurance. The Financial Ombudsman Service says so on its own site: "We can't look into every complaint we get because of the way breakdown cover is regulated. Some businesses may carry out unregulated services and we can only look at complaints about services that are regulated by the Financial Conduct Authority." It then names the products it cannot review — policy pricing, call-outs, roadside repairs and vehicle recovery — and adds, in terms: "We can't look into complaints about these issues if you're with AA, RAC or some other smaller providers."

What remains inside the Ombudsman's reach is the insured part: onward travel, repairs at a garage, overnight accommodation and incidents in Europe. So a dispute over a £535 Parts and Garage claim or an unpaid hotel bill has a free, independent route of appeal. A dispute about a patrol taking four hours, or a recovery refused as a recurring fault, or the price you were charged, does not. Complain to the AA, and if that fails the remaining options are the courts or your card provider. Anyone choosing between providers on the strength of an ombudsman backstop should know that on the headline service the backstop is not there, for the AA or for its main rivals.

sections.heading: Year two is where the real price lives
sections.html:
The 40% sale discount is explicit about its limits: online only, until 31 August 2026, new customers, first year, and only on packages that include At Home, National Recovery or Onward Travel. Roadside Assistance on its own, Parts and Garage Cover, Key Cover, Tyre Cover and Commercial Use are all excluded from it. Whatever you pay in year one, year two starts from an undiscounted base.

Ordinarily a renewing customer would be protected by the FCA's pricing rules, which since 1 January 2022 have required that a renewal quote is no higher than the price the same customer would be given as a new customer through the same channel. Those rules are written for home and motor insurance. Standalone breakdown cover is neither, so the equal-pricing protection does not apply to it, and neither does the Ombudsman — as above, pricing is one of the things it cannot examine. The practical protection is the notice period: annual members get a renewal notice before the second year begins, and monthly members must be told of a payment change at least 45 days in advance. Both are worth diarising, because on this product the only person checking the renewal price against a new-customer quote is you.

sections.heading: Charges and conditions that catch people out
sections.html:
Most cover cannot be used until 24 hours after purchase, so it is no use buying it at the roadside; Parts and Garage Cover and Key Cover need 14 days. A fault that recurs within 28 days is not covered unless the car went to a garage for permanent repair and you can show evidence of it, and repeated claims for the same problem may push the premium up. Misfuelling is not a breakdown: the AA offers a Fuel Assist service you pay for. Lost keys are the same story — locksmith costs are excluded unless Key Cover is on the policy. Breakdowns involving the emergency services after an accident, and routine maintenance, sit outside the membership altogether.

Parts and Garage Cover excludes service items, body panels, glass, keys, air conditioning unless its failure caused the breakdown, pre-existing faults, contaminated fuel damage and wear items including brake pads and clutch friction surfaces — which between them account for a good share of what actually fails on an older car. On the administrative side there is a £20 adjustment fee to cancel an unused annual policy inside the 14-day cooling-off period, 30 days' notice to come off continuous cover, £2 for a replacement card and £15 for a written VAT notification.

pros: 2,753 directly employed patrols, the largest force in the UK, attending 3.5 million breakdowns a year
8 in 10 cars repaired at the roadside on the AA's own April 2025 to March 2026 data, with a target of arriving inside the hour
Unlimited call-outs on every tier, with no annual cap on the number of attendances
Defaqto 5 Star expert rating on Roadside with National Recovery, At Home and Onward Travel
Personal cover follows you into any eligible vehicle as driver or passenger, and can carry three extra household members
Every patrol trained to Level 1 for electric vehicles and more than 98% to Level 2
No upper age limit on the vehicle, and vans, motorhomes, minibuses and motorcycles all qualify within the weight and size limits
cons: The Financial Ombudsman Service states it cannot investigate complaints about call-outs, roadside repairs, vehicle recovery or policy pricing for AA members, because those services sit outside FCA regulation — only onward travel, garage repairs, accommodation and European incidents are within its reach
The FCA's equal-pricing rule for renewals covers home and motor insurance, not standalone breakdown cover, so nothing obliges the AA to match its new-customer price at renewal
The 40% discount is first-year and new-customer only, excludes Roadside-only membership and every add-on, and ends 31 August 2026
A fault that returns within 28 days is not covered without documented evidence of a permanent garage repair, which puts the burden of proof on the member
Parts and Garage Cover pays a maximum of £535 per claim with a £35 excess and excludes wear items such as brake pads and clutch friction surfaces — much of what fails on a high-mileage car
Onward Travel is capped at three claims a year, one night's accommodation and 72 hours of hire car, and taxis are never paid for
Cancelling an unused annual policy in the cooling-off period still costs a £20 adjustment fee, and continuous cover needs 30 days' notice to stop
verdict: If what you want is the best chance of being fixed where you stand rather than towed to a garage, the AA is the strongest argument in the market: 2,753 of its own patrols, 3.5 million attendances a year and 8 in 10 cars repaired at the roadside. Bought in a sale with At Home and National Recovery attached, the first year is competitive with providers running a fraction of that capacity. The reservations are about what happens afterwards rather than what happens at the roadside — the discount is first-year only, the renewal price is not governed by the FCA rule that protects home and motor customers, and the Ombudsman cannot examine a dispute about a call-out, a recovery or a price. Treat it as a service you re-shop every year and it is very good value. Treat it as a subscription you never look at again and it will quietly cost you more than it should.

faqs.q: How soon can I use AA cover after buying it?
faqs.a: Most of the membership becomes usable 24 hours after purchase, so it cannot be bought at the side of the road to deal with a breakdown already in progress. Parts and Garage Cover and Key Cover both carry a longer 14-day wait before a claim can be made.

faqs.q: Does the AA cover a breakdown on my own driveway?
faqs.a: Only with At Home added. Standard Roadside Assistance excludes breakdowns at the registered address and within the surrounding quarter of a mile. At Home covers that area and will recover the vehicle to a nearby garage if it cannot be repaired where it sits.

faqs.q: Can I take a complaint about a slow patrol to the Financial Ombudsman?
faqs.a: No. The Ombudsman's own guidance says it cannot look into complaints about call-outs, roadside repairs, vehicle recovery or policy pricing where the provider is the AA or the RAC, because those services are not regulated by the FCA. It can consider complaints about onward travel, repairs carried out at a garage, overnight accommodation and incidents in Europe.

faqs.q: What does Onward Travel actually pay for?
faqs.a: One of three things, arranged by the AA rather than chosen by you: a mid-range saloon or hatchback hire car for up to 72 hours, one night's bed and breakfast at a hotel of the AA's choosing, or public transport for the driver and up to seven passengers to the intended destination. Taxis are excluded, and the benefit is limited to three claims in a membership year.

faqs.q: Will my price go up at renewal?
faqs.a: It can. Any introductory discount applies to the first year for new customers only, and the FCA rule requiring renewal prices to match new-customer prices applies to home and motor insurance rather than standalone breakdown cover. Annual members receive a renewal notice, and monthly members must be given at least 45 days' notice of a change to payments — both are the moment to compare against a fresh quote.

faqs.q: Which vehicles can go on the policy?
faqs.a: Petrol, diesel, electric and hydrogen cars of any age, plus vans, minibuses, motorhomes and motorcycles, provided each is under 3.5 tonnes gross weight, no more than 2.55 metres wide excluding mirrors and no more than 7 metres long. A caravan or trailer being towed at the time is covered within the same limits.

title: AA Motorbike Insurance (Europa Bike) Review
meta_title: AA Motorbike Insurance Review: Cover, Fees and Who Runs It
meta_description: AA-badged bike cover is arranged by Europa Bike: the five-insurer panel, a £20m third-party limit, the full fee list and what the policy leaves out.
intro:
The AA badge on a motorbike policy has always belonged to somebody else: Europa Bike, a Bristol broker that has done nothing but two-wheeled insurance since 1996. Companies House has the firm as Europa Group Limited, number 03279177, incorporated on 15 November 1996 under its original name of Motor Cycle Direct Insurance Services Limited and renamed on 3 December 2003. Its terms of business set out a panel of five insurers for annual motorbike policies — Highway, Aviva, Tradex, Ageas and AXA — and since 1 August 2023 every policy has carried basic legal expenses cover at no extra charge.

That specialism is the reason four household names put their own badge on Europa's paperwork. The group has arranged bike cover behind AA Motorcycle Insurance and RAC Bike Insurance, and motor cover behind Ford Insure and Vauxhall Insurance, alongside its own brands Motorcycle Direct, Onequote Direct, Ridersure and Wiser Choice. One thing has changed and it matters if you came here from a search for the AA: the AA's own motorbike page now reads “we’re sorry, the AA is no longer offering insurance for motorbikes”, followed by “if you’re an existing policyholder don’t worry – you’re still covered” and “AA Motorbike Insurance is provided by Europa Bike.” The book did not lapse; it simply lost the badge, and Europa Bike runs it directly.

What sits underneath is a straightforward specialist motor policy. Third-party property damage is covered to £20,000,000 against a statutory minimum of £1,200,000, the claims line on 0344 335 2934 is staffed 24 hours a day, and no claims bonus builds to nine years. Comprehensive, third party fire and theft, third party only and a laid-up option for a bike off the road are all sold, and the current policy booklet carries the version stamp FEB26(V), so the wording is being maintained rather than left to age.
