sections.heading: One Bristol broker, four familiar badges
sections.html:
Europa Group trades from Unit 2, West Point Row, Great Park Road, Bradley Stoke, Bristol BS32 4QG, and is authorised and regulated by the Financial Conduct Authority under firm reference 309794 — a number you can check yourself on the FCA Register. The group describes six brands of its own: Motorcycle Direct for bikes and scooters sold direct, Onequote Direct for car, van and home, Ridersure for brokers, Europa Underwriting, Wiser Choice and Wiser Choice Bike. On top of those it has run white-label programmes for the AA, the RAC, Ford and Vauxhall, and says Ford Insure alone delivered more than 500,000 policies over five years.

The AA-branded paperwork is still hosted on Europa's own servers, which is how the arrangement is visible from outside. The legal expenses wording issued with AA bike policies carries the reference LEI/AA/06/19 and names two further firms: 4th Dimension Innovation Limited of Thorpe Business Park, Egham (firm reference 516498) as administrator, and Financial and Legal Insurance Company Limited of Cheadle (firm reference 202915) as insurer. That wording covers uninsured loss recovery to £100,000 with solicitors' costs capped at £100 an hour, motor prosecution defence to £2,500, and requires a claim to be reported within 120 days of the incident. The AA page itself refers to policies purchased or renewed from 10 September 2020.

A small inconsistency is worth knowing about before you go looking for the company. The terms of business dated August 2024 still give the address as Europa House, Midland Way, Thornbury, Bristol BS35 2JX. Companies House and the current website footer both give the Bradley Stoke address. The registered number and firm reference are identical in both, so this is a move that one document has yet to catch up with rather than two different companies.

sections.heading: What the policy pays on, and where it stops
sections.html:
Liability for injury to other people is unlimited, as the Road Traffic Act requires; damage to their property is covered to £20,000,000, which is a little over sixteen times the £1,200,000 the law actually demands. Comprehensive adds accidental damage, spare parts and accessories, and recovery of the bike to the nearest approved repairer. Third party fire and theft strips that back to fire and theft losses. The laid-up option covers fire, theft and accidental damage only while the bike sits at the garaging address you declared, and drops the requirement for tax and an MOT.

New motorcycle replacement is one of the better clauses and one of the most conditional. It applies where the bike is stolen, or where repair costs run past 70% of its list price including VAT, within six months of purchase — and only if you were the first registered owner and own the bike outright or on hire purchase. Leasing and contract hire are outside it. Otherwise the settlement basis is market value, the agreed figure on your schedule or the cost of repair, whichever is lowest.

Riding abroad is allowed for 30 days per trip up to 90 days in any one period of insurance, across the EU and designated countries. No claims bonus runs to nine years with protection available, and the booklet publishes the full step-back table for up to three fault claims. The exclusions are the ordinary ones for the class: helmets, leathers and personal belongings are not covered by the policy itself, theft is excluded where the keys were left in the ignition, and unauthorised use by someone known to you is excluded unless you report it to the police. Defence costs after a death on the road are capped at £1,000 for any one occurrence, which is modest next to the £2,500 in the separate legal expenses wording.

sections.heading: Six add-ons, and what each one is worth
sections.html:
Because the core policy leaves out protective kit and most of the legal cost of an accident, the optional list is where a lot of the value sits:

  • Legal expenses: up to £100,000 for non-fault claims, including personal injury and motoring defence. The basic version has been included free on policies since 1 August 2023.
  • Helmet and leathers: up to £1,000 for protective gear damaged in an accident — the gap the main policy leaves.
  • Personal accident: up to £25,000 for injury, disability or death.
  • Replacement vehicle: a hire bike of up to 650cc for up to 14 days after an accident, theft or vandalism.
  • Excess Protect: refunds the excess up to £600 a year on accidental damage, fire, theft, vandalism and flood claims.
  • Key Protect: up to £1,500 towards locksmiths and immobiliser reprogramming for lost, stolen or broken keys.

Discounts are offered for no claims history, secure parking and riding experience. Europa is paid a flat fee by the insurer for arranging the optional extras, which is disclosed in the terms of business rather than buried.

sections.heading: The fee schedule, in full
sections.html:
This is a non-advised sale: the terms of business say plainly “you will not receive advice or a recommendation from us”, and the firm acts as your agent in arranging the insurance while acting as the insurer's agent when collecting premiums and paying refunds. Premiums are treated as held by the insurer under risk transfer, and any interest earned on them is kept by Europa Group. Commission is taken from the insurer as a percentage that varies with the bike and the rider, plus a percentage of the loan where the premium is paid monthly through the group's credit provider.

The charges published in the August 2024 document are:

  • Renewal: up to £75
  • Mid-term change: £40 through the contact centre, £20 through the online portal
  • Cancelling inside the 14-day cooling-off period: £40
  • Cancelling after it, where the policy came from a price comparison site: £75
  • Cancelling after it, where it did not: £40
  • Policy voided for misrepresentation: £75
  • Duplicate documents: £10
  • Correcting a new business error: free

Paying monthly costs more than paying in one go, which the document states rather than leaving you to work out. The cooling-off period runs 14 days from the start of the policy or the day you receive the documents, whichever is later. Europa Group is covered by both the Financial Ombudsman Service and the Financial Services Compensation Scheme, and takes complaints at crt@europa-group.co.uk.

sections.heading: Its own complaints numbers are published, and they are not flattering
sections.html:
Europa Group publishes its complaints return on its own website, which most brokers do not, and the figures for 1 January to 30 June 2026 are worth reading before you buy. It opened 215 complaints and closed 209. Of those, 102 were closed inside three days and 107 took longer than three days but under eight weeks. None took more than eight weeks, which is a genuinely good result. But 44% were upheld — the firm agreed the customer was right in nearly half the cases it decided — and the total redress paid on all upheld complaints was £3,562, against £1,221 paid out on complaints it rejected. Spread across roughly 92 upheld cases, that is an average of about £39 each.

For scale, the Financial Ombudsman Service's annual data published on 21 May 2026 recorded 13,420 new complaints about car or motorcycle insurance in 2025/26, upheld at 35%, within 214,600 complaints across all financial products at an average uphold rate of 30%. A 44% uphold rate at the firm's own first stage sits above that, though the two are not measuring quite the same thing: a broker's internal figure counts service and administration disputes that never reach the ombudsman.

The wider value picture comes from the FCA's general insurance value measures data for calendar year 2025, published on 21 July 2026. Motor claims costs rose to 59% of premium from 54% the year before while premiums fell 7% and policies in force grew 4%, and the motor claims acceptance rate stands at 99%. Motorcycle is not itemised separately in that release, so there is no bike-specific acceptance rate to hold any insurer against.

sections.heading: The risk the premium is actually pricing
sections.html:
Bike premiums look punishing next to car premiums until you look at the casualty rates. The Department for Transport's motorcyclist factsheet, published on 30 July 2026, records 386 motorcyclists killed on Britain's roads in 2025 and 5,710 seriously injured, 6,096 killed or seriously injured in total. The fatality rate works out at 128 per billion vehicle miles and the serious injury rate at 1,891. Across 2021 to 2025, 92% of motorcycle KSI casualties were male and 62% of fatalities happened away from junctions on rural roads. The rate has improved — down 37% across all severities since 2004 — but it remains an order of magnitude above car travel.

Demand is going the other way. Motorcycle Industry Association registrations to May 2026 were running 15.8% ahead of the same point in 2025, with adventure bikes up 24.8% year to date and road sport up 16.9%. Meanwhile the Association of British Insurers reported on 29 July 2026 that insurers paid a record £3.2 billion in motor claims in the second quarter, with the average claim up 4% to £4,900 and the average motor premium paid rising £6 to £566. More riders, dearer repairs and a casualty rate like that is the arithmetic behind every bike quote you will be given this year.

pros: Motorcycle-only specialist since 1996, and the firm actually behind AA, RAC, Ford and Vauxhall-badged cover
Third-party property damage to £20,000,000, against a legal minimum of £1,200,000
Basic legal expenses cover included free on policies since 1 August 2023
Claims line staffed 24 hours a day, seven days a week
Not one complaint took longer than eight weeks to close in the first half of 2026
Laid-up cover available for a bike off the road, without needing tax or an MOT
New motorcycle replacement within six months where repairs pass 70% of list price
cons: The AA has stopped selling motorbike insurance altogether, and the Europa Bike site now leads to a customer portal for existing policyholders rather than a quote form — new riders are pushed towards the group's Motorcycle Direct brand instead
44% of the 209 complaints closed between January and June 2026 were upheld, and the total redress paid on them came to £3,562, an average of roughly £39
No excess figures appear in the policy booklet or the summary document — the wording says only that the amount is shown on your schedule, so you cannot compare it before you quote
The fee schedule is steep for a bike policy: up to £75 to renew, £75 to cancel if you bought through a price comparison site, £40 for a phone amendment and £10 for a duplicate document
Helmets, leathers and personal belongings are excluded from the policy itself and only covered by buying the £1,000 add-on
No sales or service telephone number is published — contact runs through live chat, Monday to Friday 9am to 6pm and Saturday 9am to 1pm
The published documents are out of step with each other: a summary dated August 2023, terms of business from August 2024 carrying a superseded Thornbury address, and a booklet stamped FEB26(V)
verdict: Europa Bike is a competent motorcycle specialist that has spent three decades doing one thing, and the policy behind the AA badge is a reasonable one: a £20,000,000 third-party limit, a five-insurer panel, free basic legal cover and a 24-hour claims line. The catch is that the badge has gone. The AA no longer sells bike insurance, Europa Bike's own site now serves existing policyholders rather than new ones, and a rider looking for a fresh quote from this firm needs its Motorcycle Direct brand instead. Existing AA policyholders are still covered and should read the fee list before their renewal lands: at up to £75 to renew and £75 to cancel, the administration can move the price as much as the risk does.

faqs.q: Can I still buy AA motorbike insurance?
faqs.a: No. The AA's own motorbike page states that it is no longer offering insurance for motorbikes. Existing policies remain in force and Europa Bike, which arranged them, now looks after the book directly. If you want a new quote from the same firm, it sells under its Motorcycle Direct brand.

faqs.q: Who underwrites the cover?
faqs.a: Europa Group Limited is a broker, not an insurer. Its terms of business name a panel of five insurers for annual motorbike policies: Highway, Aviva, Tradex, Ageas and AXA. The policy booklet does not name the insurer at all, referring only to “the insurer described in your schedule”, so you will not know which of the five you have until the documents arrive.

faqs.q: What is the excess?
faqs.a: It is not published. Both the policy booklet and the insurance product information document confirm that an excess applies but state the amount is shown on your individual schedule. Ask for it in writing before you accept a quote, and ask separately about any additional excess for young or newly qualified riders.

faqs.q: How long can I ride abroad on the policy?
faqs.a: Thirty days per trip, up to a maximum of 90 days in any one period of insurance, across Great Britain, Northern Ireland, the Channel Islands, the Isle of Man and EU or designated countries.

faqs.q: Is Europa Bike properly regulated?
faqs.a: Europa Group Limited is authorised and regulated by the Financial Conduct Authority under firm reference 309794 and registered in England and Wales as company 03279177. It is covered by both the Financial Ombudsman Service and the Financial Services Compensation Scheme. The firm reference is verifiable on the FCA Register.

faqs.q: What does it cost to change or cancel a policy?
faqs.a: The August 2024 terms of business set a mid-term change at £40 through the contact centre or £20 online, cancellation at £40 inside the 14-day cooling-off period, £40 afterwards, or £75 afterwards if the policy came from a price comparison site. A voided policy costs £75 and duplicate documents £10. Insurer charges may apply on top.

title: AA Van Insurance Review
meta_title: AA Van Insurance Review: Cover, Fees and Its 4 Insurers
meta_description: The AA arranges van cover from four named insurers. What its own contract document says about fees, class of use and the price promise at renewal.
intro:
Van insurance from the AA is arranged by Automobile Association Insurance Services Limited, a broker holding Financial Conduct Authority firm reference 310562, verifiable on the FCA Register. It is a big operation by any measure. The company's own published complaints statement counts 2,763,187 insurance policies sold in the six months from 1 August 2025 to 31 January 2026, and its filed accounts for the year to 31 January 2025 show revenue of £295m, up from £265m the year before.

The useful thing about the AA on vans is that it names its underwriters in writing. Its van contract document, dated July 2025, lists a panel of four: Ageas Insurance Limited, Aviva Insurance Limited, Covéa Insurance plc and Highway Insurance Company Limited. Whichever of those four prices your risk is printed on the quote before you buy, which is more than most van sites will tell you. Comprehensive cover comes with windscreen repair or replacement that does not cost you your no claims discount, an uninsured driver promise that waives the excess and protects the discount if an identified uninsured driver hits you, personal belongings cover and a UK claims line open around the clock on 0330 053 0322.

Sitting over the top of all four is the AA's Fair Price Promise: "When it's time to renew, we promise you won't pay more than if you were a new customer." For a van that phrase carries more weight than it does on a car, for a reason set out further down this page. Cover runs from third party only through third party, fire and theft to comprehensive, drivers aged 18 to 99 are eligible, and up to four additional named drivers can go on the policy. A quote holds for 28 days and cover can be bought up to 30 days before it starts.

sections.heading: Four insurers behind one badge, and what each of them brings
sections.html:
The AA does not carry the risk on a van policy. It finds an insurer, sets the policy up and administers it, and takes a share of the premium for doing so. Its van contract document says plainly that the firm is "not able to provide you with a personal recommendation on which insurance or optional additional products you should purchase", and that it acts for the insurer rather than for you: "We act for our insurer(s) in marketing their products and we are authorised to act for the insurer when entering into a contract of insurance with you on their behalf." Premium and claims money is handled as the insurer's agent, which is the arrangement that protects you if the broker fails before the money reaches the underwriter.

Knowing the four names lets you read the actual cover before you buy. Highway Insurance Company Limited publishes its van product document under FCA reference 202972, and the numbers in it are the numbers you would be buying: third-party injury cover unlimited, third-party property damage up to £5,000,000, personal accident benefit of £5,000 for the policyholder and partner, personal belongings up to £300, replacement locks up to £500, non-factory-fitted in-vehicle equipment up to £500, and audio equipment capped at £150 on third party, fire and theft. Driving abroad runs to 37 European countries at the minimum cover the law there requires, not the comprehensive cover you hold at home. Theft is not paid if the van was left unlocked, or with the keys in it and the engine running — the single exclusion that catches more multi-drop drivers than any other.

sections.heading: The three fees, and where in the price each one hides
sections.html:
The AA's van contract document sets out the charges in one place, which not every broker does. A £28 arrangement fee is "included in the agreed price", so it does not appear as a separate line and it is already inside the figure on the quote. A £25 admin fee applies to any policy change made over the phone or through webchat, and no fee at all applies to the same change made in the online account — a genuine saving for anyone who changes a registration or an address more than once a year. Cancelling costs £32.50.

The cooling-off period is 14 days from the later of receiving the documents or entering the contract. Inside it, a policy that has not started yet gets a full premium refund; one that has started gets the premium back less a deduction for the days on cover. The fees are kept either way, and a policy with a claim on it gets nothing back. The Financial Services Compensation Scheme covers the arranging of van insurance at 90% of a claim with no upper limit, and the compulsory third-party element in full.

If a claim goes wrong, complaints go to Customer Solutions, The AA, Park Square, Birdhall Lane, Cheadle SK3 0XN, or to 0344 209 0556, and then to the Financial Ombudsman Service. That last step is worth a moment. In the Ombudsman's annual data published 21 May 2026, covering 214,600 new complaints across every financial product at an average uphold rate of 30%, commercial vehicle insurance produced 1,429 complaints and the Ombudsman found for the customer in 44% of them — against 35% on car and motorcycle policies, from 13,420 complaints. Van disputes are the ones the Ombudsman is most likely to decide against the insurer.

sections.heading: Class of use decides the price, the cover and the rules that apply
sections.html:
The AA offers three classes: social, domestic and commuting; carriage of own goods; and haulage. Picking the wrong one is the most common way a van claim is refused, because carrying anything for payment on a social-and-commuting policy is uninsured driving. Carriage of own goods covers tools and stock belonging to your own business. Haulage covers goods belonging to somebody else, and prices accordingly.

That choice has a second consequence almost nobody flags. The FCA's pricing rules, in force since 1 January 2022, stop an insurer charging a renewing customer more than an equivalent new customer. They apply to consumer home and motor policies, and the FCA extended them to owners of commercial vehicles such as vans and pickups only where the vehicle is used for social, domestic and pleasure purposes. A van insured for carriage of own goods or haulage sits outside them. Pick either of the business classes and the legal protection against a walk-up renewal price disappears — which is exactly why the AA's Fair Price Promise is worth reading properly on a van. On a business-use van it is not the regulator's floor being restated. It is a voluntary commitment doing a job no rule is doing, and it is the strongest single argument for the AA over a cheaper name that makes no such promise.

Some context for what is being priced. SMMT's Motorparc figures published 24 April 2026 put 5,175,598 vans on UK roads at the end of 2025, up 1.4% in the year and up 29.2% since 2015 — faster growth than any other vehicle type. Battery electric vans passed 113,256, or 2.2% of the fleet. The ABI's motor figures published 29 July 2026 show insurers paying a record £3.2bn in claims in the second quarter of 2026, an average premium of £566, an average claim of £4,900 and windscreen repairs alone averaging £283. Against a £4,900 average claim, choosing a £500 voluntary excess to shave the premium is a real bet, not a formality.

sections.heading: What the add-ons actually pay for
sections.html:
Four extras can be bolted on. Van Legal Assistance pursues uninsured losses — the excess, lost earnings, injury — that the motor policy itself will not pay. Van Hire provides a replacement for up to 28 days, limited to two claims in a policy year, which is the add-on that matters most if the van is how you earn. Tools in Transit also allows two claims a year, sharing one combined limit between them; the limit is set at quote and is worth checking against what is genuinely in the back, because a full plumber's or sparks' kit outruns a typical cap quickly. Breakdown Cover is capped at three call-outs a policy year, which is a meaningfully thinner product than the AA's standalone membership, where roadside call-outs are unlimited. Anyone buying an AA van policy mainly to get AA recovery should price the membership separately rather than assume the add-on is the same thing.

Two discounts are worth asking about. A GPS tracker can take up to 10% off, and a higher voluntary excess — selectable up to £500 — will move the price, though the insurer's compulsory excess sits underneath it and can rise again for younger drivers or heavier vehicles.

sections.heading: Three things to weigh before you click through
sections.html:
The first is the size of the panel. Four insurers is a narrow shortlist for a market this large, and it is narrow by the AA's own standards — its car contract document runs to roughly 13 insurers. A four-name panel will not always find the cheapest van premium, and since the sale is non-advised nobody at the AA will tell you when it has not. Running the same details through a broader panel before committing costs nothing but time.

The second is the evidence gap on this specific product. The AA publishes a Defaqto 5 Star rating for Gold and Platinum comprehensive car insurance and for Platinum home insurance, and quotes a hard price benchmark for car — 10% of customers paying £265 or less, on new business from February to July 2026. There is no published Defaqto rating for AA van insurance and no equivalent van price figure on the site. The AA's own complaints table for the period is loaded by script and does not render as text, so the complaint volumes and uphold rates behind that 2,763,187 policy count could not be read directly and need confirming with the AA. The FCA's value measures data published 21 July 2026 covers motor as a whole — a 99% claims acceptance rate and claims costs at 59% of premium, up from 54% — but does not break vans out, so there is no van-specific acceptance rate to hold any of the four insurers against.

The third is that one of the four underwriters is about to change its name. Highway Insurance Company Limited is one of the entities transferring into Allianz Insurance plc under a Part VII scheme of the Financial Services and Markets Act 2000, with a High Court sanction hearing listed for 2 October 2026 and an effective date of 1 January 2027. Policy terms carry across a Part VII transfer unchanged and there is nothing for a policyholder to do, but anyone quoted on Highway should expect the Allianz name on their renewal and should read the scheme documents if they want the detail rather than the summary.

pros: Names all four panel insurers in writing, so the underwriter and its published limits can be checked before buying
Fair Price Promise caps the renewal at the new-customer price, which matters most on business-use vans that FCA pricing rules do not cover
Windscreen repair or replacement without losing the no claims discount, on comprehensive
Uninsured driver promise refunds the excess and protects the discount where the other driver is identified and uninsured
Policy changes made in the online account carry no admin fee, against £25 by phone or webchat
Haulage as well as carriage of own goods is quoted, which several direct insurers will not touch
Up to 10% off where a GPS tracker is fitted, and four named drivers included
Wide eligibility: drivers from 18 to 99, with UK, EU or foreign licences accepted
cons: Only four insurers on the van panel, against roughly 13 on the AA's own car panel, so the cheapest van premium in the market will often sit outside it
The sale is non-advised and the AA acts as agent of the insurer, not of you, so nobody is obliged to tell you the panel has been beaten elsewhere

£28 arrangement fee is folded into the quoted price rather than shown separately, £25 to change anything by phone or webchat, £32.50 to cancel — and all of it is kept even if you cancel inside the 14-day cooling-off period
No published Defaqto rating and no van price benchmark, while AA car and home insurance get both
Breakdown as an add-on is capped at three call-outs a year, far thinner than the unlimited roadside call-outs on standalone AA membership
Highway policyholders will see their underwriter become Allianz Insurance plc on 1 January 2027 under a Part VII transfer
Commercial vehicle insurance carries a 44% Ombudsman uphold rate against 35% for cars, so van claims disputes are more often decided against the insurer
verdict: The AA is a broker on vans, not an insurer, and it is unusually straight about it — the four panel insurers are named, the three fees are written down, and the basis of sale is spelled out. That transparency is the reason to start here. The Fair Price Promise is the strongest part of the offer and is worth more on a van than on a car, because a van insured for carriage of own goods or haulage sits outside the FCA rules that would otherwise cap a renewal. Set against that, four insurers is a short panel, the fees are real and non-refundable, and there is no van-specific quality rating to check. Worth a quote, particularly for own-goods and haulage use, and worth putting a broader panel alongside it before you buy.

faqs.q: Who underwrites AA van insurance?
faqs.a: One of four insurers named in the AA's van contract document dated July 2025: Ageas Insurance Limited, Aviva Insurance Limited, Covéa Insurance plc or Highway Insurance Company Limited. Which one you get is shown on the quote before you buy. Highway is transferring into Allianz Insurance plc on 1 January 2027 under a Part VII scheme, with a sanction hearing listed for 2 October 2026.

faqs.q: What does the AA charge in fees on a van policy?
faqs.a: A £28 arrangement fee is built into the quoted price rather than added on top. Changing the policy costs £25 by phone or webchat and nothing through the online account. Cancelling costs £32.50. Inside the 14-day cooling-off period the premium is refunded in full if cover has not started, or less a charge for time on cover if it has, but the fees are kept in both cases.

faqs.q: Does the Fair Price Promise apply to a business-use van?
faqs.a: The AA states the promise without carving out business use: "When it's time to renew, we promise you won't pay more than if you were a new customer." It is worth understanding why that matters on a van. The FCA's pricing rules, in force since 1 January 2022, reach commercial vehicles only where they are used for social, domestic and pleasure purposes, so a van rated for carriage of own goods or haulage has no regulatory protection against a higher renewal price. Confirm at the quote stage that the promise is being applied to your class of use.

faqs.q: Is the AA breakdown add-on the same as AA membership?
faqs.a: No. The van insurance add-on is limited to three call-outs in a policy year. Standalone AA breakdown membership has no cap on roadside call-outs. If recovery is the main reason for choosing the AA, price the membership on its own rather than relying on the add-on.

faqs.q: What class of use should I pick?
faqs.a: Social, domestic and commuting covers personal journeys and the trip to a single place of work, and nothing carried for payment. Carriage of own goods covers tools, stock and materials belonging to your own business. Haulage covers goods belonging to somebody else. Carrying anything for payment on a social-and-commuting policy leaves you uninsured, so pick up rather than down.

faqs.q: Where do I complain if a van claim goes wrong?
faqs.a: First to the AA, on 0344 209 0556, by email to insurance.complaints@theAA.com, or in writing to Customer Solutions, The AA, Park Square, Birdhall Lane, Cheadle SK3 0XN. If that does not resolve it, the Financial Ombudsman Service will look at it free of charge. Ombudsman data published on 21 May 2026 shows commercial vehicle complaints upheld at 44%, above the 30% average across all financial products.

title: Towergate Boat Insurance
meta_title: Towergate Boat Insurance Review: £5m Cover, New Name
meta_description: Towergate's marine book is now Navigators & General — a 1921 specialist with £5m liability as standard. What moved, what stayed, and what the wording pays.
intro:
Ask for Towergate boat insurance today and you will be dealing with Navigators & General, a Brighton marine specialist that has been writing pleasure craft since 1921. That is not a rebadged call centre: the desk has been quoting yachts, narrowboats, sports boats and dinghies for a hundred and five years, spent forty-one of them inside Zurich after a 1983 acquisition, and moved to The Ardonagh Group in 2024. Most of the staff sail, row or cruise something themselves, which shows in the range — twelve separate products covering everything from a canoe to a commercial workboat.

The standard cover is strong for the money. Third party liability runs to £5 million on yachts, motorboats, sailing craft and small craft, and £3 million of third party and passenger liability on inland waterways. Rescue and evacuation is covered to £50,000, and there is another £50,000 for family and guests hit by an uninsured vessel. Machinery damage is included from new as standard where you can show routine maintenance, tenders stay covered even when used on their own, and an RYA qualification can take up to 10% off the price. Park in a marina and the excess disappears; prove the other party was at fault and it disappears again.

Two things changed underneath the brand and neither was announced loudly. The risk stopped sitting with Zurich on 1 December 2024, and from 1 November 2025 every Towergate marine policy moved to Geo Underwriting Services Limited, trading as Navigators & General. The Towergate name itself was retired across the group on 17 November 2025 in favour of Everywhen. The same team answers the phone on 01242 531172, the cover is largely the same cover, but the names on your certificate are not the names you bought from — and that matters more than it sounds when you come to claim.

sections.heading: Three names between you and the money
sections.html:
Follow the chain and it runs four deep. You buy from Navigators & General, which is a trading name of Geo Underwriting Services Limited, authorised and regulated by the Financial Conduct Authority under firm reference 308400 and registered at 2 Minster Court, Mincing Lane, London EC3R 7PD. Geo is the managing general agent — it prices the risk, issues the documents and handles the claim, but the money behind the policy belongs to HCC International Insurance Company plc, trading as Tokio Marine HCC, which holds firm reference 202655 and is regulated by both the FCA and the Prudential Regulation Authority. If you take the optional legal expenses cover, that section is arranged by Arc Legal Assistance and underwritten by AmTrust Specialty Limited under firm reference 202189, so a legal claim goes somewhere different again.

The Towergate side has moved too. Towergate branded policies sat with Advisory Insurance Brokers Limited, firm reference 313250, company number 4043759, which now trades as Everywhen after the group retired the Towergate name on 17 November 2025. The rebrand covered more than thirty-five broking businesses carrying roughly £2 billion of gross written premium and over 500,000 customers across more than 100 UK offices. Type the old Towergate boat address into a browser and you land on an Everywhen page whose only real function is a button reading "Go to Navigators & General". Existing Towergate marine policies keep their old branding until renewal and then come out the other side as Navigators & General documents.

None of that changes your protection. Both firms are FCA regulated, the policy carries Financial Services Compensation Scheme cover, and eligible complaints reach the Financial Ombudsman Service after eight weeks or a final response, whichever comes first. It does change who you ring, and it means a policy schedule from 2023 and a policy schedule from 2026 will name different companies for the same boat.

sections.heading: Agreed value is less agreed than it sounds
sections.html:
Marine insurance is usually sold on the promise that you fix the boat's worth in advance rather than argue about depreciation after a sinking. Navigators & General offers agreed value across its pleasure craft range, and it is worth having. Read the Freedom Sailing wording, though, and the default basis is market value — the cost of replacing the vessel with allowance for type, age and wear — with agreed value sitting as an option in Part B of the policy. Whether you actually bought it will be printed on your schedule and nowhere else, so that line is worth finding before you need it.

Even with agreed value selected, the deduction does not go away entirely. The wording states that deductions for age are made on any life rafts, tenders, outboards and trailers at 10% a year up to a maximum of 50%. A five-year-old outboard on an agreed-value policy is therefore a half-price outboard. The same logic runs through the general settlement clause: old materials are replaced with new without a betterment cut, except for sails, protective covers, running rigging, outboard motors, batteries and personal belongings, where the insurer may reduce the claim for age and condition. Those are precisely the items most likely to be damaged.

Personal belongings carry their own ceilings — £300 for any single item, rising to £750 if the boat is your home — and cover for contents stops if the vessel is left unoccupied for more than 45 days in a row. Theft of a tender doubles your excess unless the tender carries a permanent unique identifier. There are useful small benefits pulling the other way: key cover pays up to £500 a claim and £2,000 a year with no excess, and a lockout pays £60 an incident.

sections.heading: The line on your schedule that decides a claim
sections.html:
Cruising limits do more work in marine insurance than any other clause, and this policy runs five of them. Non-tidal UK waters covers inland systems only, with tidal stretches permitted purely to get in and out. Coastal UK waters reaches 12 nautical miles offshore. The continental Brest to Elbe range adds the near continent but forbids anything north of 61 degrees. Elbe to La Rochelle moves its southern boundary with the calendar — 48 degrees north between October and March, 46 degrees north from April to September. The European inland and coastal option holds you to 5 miles offshore. Weather, danger or an order from a government or legal authority are the only permitted reasons to cross the line.

Inland waterways policies work differently again. They are British inland waters only, with no continental extension, but they include up to 30 days of UK coastal use in a policy year at no extra charge, and free personal accident cover to £60,000 for one event covering the owner and non-paying guests. Liveaboard cover extends household belongings, alternative accommodation and £3 million of liability to members of the household.

Some restrictions sit outside the geography. The third party product declines vessels built before 1960, anything capable of more than 50 knots, ferro cement hulls, static houseboats and amateur-built or converted craft. Surveys are generally required on boats over 23 feet and more than 20 years old, and once one is done satisfactorily no further survey is asked for at least five years. Machinery breakdown cover attaches to newer hulls, and here the marketing and the wording do not quite line up: the product pages say cover runs for up to three years from new as standard, while the Freedom Sailing wording conditions that section on the vessel being under five years old from completion of build.

sections.heading: Where the small print will catch you out
sections.html:
Sail alone and read this twice. You are not covered single handed for more than 18 hours in any 24 hour period, and not covered single handed at all if the vessel is over 10 metres, unless the schedule is endorsed to say otherwise. Racing is excluded for masts, spars, fittings, sails and rigging unless Racing Risks has been bought in Part B, though the underwriter will look at events, racing weeks and RORC or JOG entries on referral.

The exclusions read like a surveyor's report. Osmosis, marine growth and gradual water ingress are out. So is gradual deterioration, unless it could not have been spotted by routine inspection or prevented by servicing and maintenance in line with an engineer's, surveyor's or manufacturer's advice — a clause that puts your maintenance record on trial. Machinery failure caused solely by the breakdown of a component part is excluded. Personal accident cover stops entirely at age 75, and medical expenses under the sailing wording pay £500 for any one incident, where the motorboat product page advertises up to £1,000 following an accident on board.

Excess figures are the real gap. Nothing published names a number: the wording refers you to the schedule throughout, so the excess only becomes visible once you have a quote in hand. There is no retail fee schedule on the site either, so instalment charges, mid-term adjustment fees and cancellation costs are not knowable before you engage. A total loss carries no excess, marina and ashore claims carry none, and a proven non-fault claim carries none, which is genuinely good — but the number that applies the rest of the time is yours to extract on the phone.

sections.heading: How to check them, and what nobody publishes
sections.html:
The Financial Ombudsman Service published its 2025/26 annual data on 21 May 2026, recording 214,600 new complaints across all financial products and an average uphold rate of 30%. Pleasure craft is not one of the product lines it breaks out, so there is no boat insurance uphold rate to hold this insurer against — a limitation worth knowing rather than a criticism of the firm. The 14 day cooling-off period applies from the day the documents arrive, and gives a full premium refund provided you have not claimed and do not intend to. Watch the automatic renewal clause if you pay by credit agreement, because consenting to the credit consents to the roll-over.

Two claims made about this insurer could not be verified from outside a quote. No current Defaqto star rating for the pleasure craft range could be found on the provider's own material, so treat any starred badge you see elsewhere as needing confirmation. A multi-vessel or fleet discount is widely assumed to exist for owners with more than one boat, but nothing on the provider's public pages or in the broker product brochure sets out the terms, so ask for it in writing rather than expecting it. Twelve month laid-up policies at reduced rates are confirmed for boats out of use, and small craft moorings allow up to 28 days between April and September.

Before buying, get three things in writing: the excess that applies to a hull damage claim, whether agreed value or market value is showing on your schedule, and the exact cruising range against where you actually intend to go. Then quote it against Craftinsure, GJW Direct and Haven Knox-Johnston, because the pleasure craft market is small enough that the same hull can attract very different numbers.

pros: A genuine marine specialist since 1921, with 105 years of pleasure craft underwriting behind the quote
£5 million third party liability as standard on yacht, motorboat, sailing and small craft policies
No excess at all on a total loss, on claims in a marina berth or ashore, or on a proven non-fault claim
£50,000 rescue and evacuation and a further £50,000 if an uninsured vessel hits your family or guests
Tenders covered even when used independently of the parent vessel
Twelve product lines covering canoes, paddleboards, rowing boats, RIBs, narrowboats, yachts and commercial craft
Up to 10% off for an RYA qualification
Inland waterways policies include 30 days of UK coastal use a year at no extra charge
Key cover to £500 a claim and £2,000 a year, and £60 for a lockout, both with no excess
FSCS protection and Financial Ombudsman access both confirmed in the wording
cons: Agreed value does not stop age deductions: life rafts, tenders, outboards and trailers lose 10% a year to a maximum of 50%, even on an agreed-value policy
Market value is the default settlement basis and agreed value is an optional Part B upgrade, so the headline promise depends on a line on your schedule
No excess figure is published anywhere — the wording defers to the schedule throughout, so you cannot compare the real cost of a claim before quoting
No retail fee schedule is published, leaving instalment, mid-term adjustment and cancellation charges invisible until you engage
Sails, covers, running rigging, outboards and batteries are all exposed to age and condition deductions on any claim
Cover for contents stops if the boat is left unoccupied for more than 45 days in a row
Single handed use is limited to 18 hours in any 24, and barred entirely above 10 metres, without an endorsement
Personal accident cover ends at age 75

Marketing and wording disagree in two places: machinery cover is described as three years from new but conditioned on the boat being under five years old, and medical expenses are advertised up to £1,000 while the sailing wording pays £500 an incident
The underwriter changed on 1 December 2024 and the administrator on 1 November 2025, so a claim on an older policy may involve companies you never bought from
Searching for Towergate boat insurance now lands on an Everywhen signpost page rather than a quote form, adding a hop before you reach the product
No current Defaqto rating for the pleasure craft range could be found on the provider's own material
verdict: A century-old marine specialist wearing a new set of names. The cover itself is competitive — £5 million of liability as standard, £50,000 for rescue and evacuation, no excess in a marina or on a total loss, tenders covered independently and up to 10% off for an RYA ticket — and the 1921 pedigree is real rather than marketing. The changes are administrative: Zurich stepped back from the risk on 1 December 2024, Tokio Marine HCC carries it now under firm reference 202655, and the Towergate marine book moved to Geo Underwriting on 1 November 2025 before the Towergate brand itself was retired that same month. What deserves your attention is not the branding but the wording. Agreed value still depreciates outboards, tenders and life rafts at 10% a year to a 50% floor, no excess figure is published anywhere on the public site, single handed cover stops at 18 hours and at 10 metres, and the cruising range on your certificate is the clause that will decide a claim. Get the excess, the valuation basis and the cruising limits confirmed in writing, then quote it against Craftinsure, GJW Direct and Haven Knox-Johnston before you commit.

faqs.q: Is Towergate boat insurance still available?
faqs.a: Not under that name. The Towergate marine book transferred to Geo Underwriting Services Limited, trading as Navigators & General, on 1 November 2025, and the Towergate brand was retired across the group on 17 November 2025 in favour of Everywhen. Existing policies keep their Towergate branding until renewal, then convert. The team is reachable on 01242 531172.

faqs.q: Who actually underwrites the policy now?
faqs.a: HCC International Insurance Company plc, trading as Tokio Marine HCC, under firm reference 202655. Navigators & General is a trading name of Geo Underwriting Services Limited, firm reference 308400, which acts as the managing general agent. Policies written before 1 December 2024 sat with Zurich instead.

faqs.q: How much third party liability do I get?
faqs.a: £5 million as standard on yacht, motorboat, sailing and small craft policies, and £3 million of third party and passenger liability on inland waterways cover, which extends to household members on a liveaboard extension. Marinas, harbours and recognised mooring areas generally require evidence of third party cover before they will take your lines.

faqs.q: Does agreed value mean I get the full sum insured?
faqs.a: Not on everything. Agreed value fixes the vessel's figure, but the wording still deducts 10% a year, up to a maximum of 50%, from life rafts, tenders, outboards and trailers. Sails, protective covers, running rigging, batteries and personal belongings can also be reduced for age and condition. Check whether your schedule shows agreed value or market value, because market value is the default.

faqs.q: Will I need a survey?
faqs.a: Generally yes if the boat is over 23 feet and more than 20 years old. Once a survey has been completed satisfactorily, no further survey is normally requested for at least five years. Machinery cover is aimed at newer hulls, so an older boat should expect hull and liability cover rather than breakdown protection.

faqs.q: How far can I sail on a standard policy?
faqs.a: It depends which of the five cruising ranges is on your schedule. UK coastal reaches 12 nautical miles offshore. Brest to Elbe adds the near continent but bars anything above 61 degrees north. Elbe to La Rochelle runs to 48 degrees north from October to March and 46 degrees north from April to September. European inland and coastal holds you to 5 miles offshore. Inland waterways policies are British inland waters plus 30 days of UK coastal use.

faqs.q: What if I have a complaint?
faqs.a: The internal route aims to resolve within three business days, escalating to the Customer Relations Unit with a response inside eight weeks. After that, or after a final response, eligible customers can take it to the Financial Ombudsman Service at Exchange Tower, London E14 9SR, on 0800 023 4567. The policy also carries Financial Services Compensation Scheme protection.

title: Voyager Travel Insurance Review
meta_title: Voyager Travel Insurance Review: Limits, Tiers & Fees 2026
meta_description: Voyager Plus in full: four tiers, a £150 excess falling to £50, £10m medical, 100+ activities as standard and a high-risk sister brand.
intro:
Voyager includes more than 100 sports and activities as standard, each published with its own depth, altitude or river grade rather than hidden behind the phrase ‘hazardous activity’. The firm has been arranging travel cover since September 1996, and for most of that time it did not sell to the public at all — it placed wholesale schemes for tour operators, which is why the policy wording reads like something written for people who already know what a grade 3 river is. Its retail brand, Voyager Plus, now sells single trip, annual multi-trip and long stay cover directly, and in February 2024 it bought Navigator Travel Insurance, a specialist it had worked alongside for more than twenty years.

The numbers at the top end are competitive. Emergency medical expenses run to £10 million on the two upper tiers, the excess on the highest tier is £50, and single trip cover carries no upper age limit. Long stay policies run to 24 months for travellers under 50. Buying or amending online carries no administration fee at all.

What sets Voyager apart is the edge of its appetite. Where a supermarket policy stops at a vague exclusion, Voyager publishes the metre and the grade — and it runs a separate brand, High Risk Voyager, for people travelling to countries the Foreign, Commonwealth & Development Office tells them to avoid. That is a narrow specialism, and it is worded and priced as one.

sections.heading: The four tiers, side by side
sections.html:
Voyager Plus is one product sold at four prices, and the gap between cheapest and dearest is wide enough that the tier matters more than the brand. Reading across Standard, Enhanced, Prime and Supreme in the 2025/26 wording, which covers departures up to 30 September 2027:

  • Excess per claim: £150, £100, £75 and £50
  • Cancellation and curtailment: £1,000, £2,500, £5,000 and £10,000
  • Emergency medical expenses: £5 million, £7.5 million, £10 million and £10 million
  • Baggage: £1,000, £1,500, £2,500 and £3,500, with single article caps of £100, £200, £300 and £400
  • Personal money: £350, £750, £1,250 and £1,500
  • Missed departure: £250, £500, £750 and £1,000
  • Travel delay: £100, £200, £250 and £500 per full 12 hours
  • Personal liability: £1 million, £2 million, £2 million and £3 million
  • Legal expenses: £10,000, £10,000, £20,000 and £35,000
  • Personal accident on death: £5,000, £7,500, £10,000 and £15,000, rising to £10,000–£35,000 for loss of limb or sight

Emergency dental is capped at £500 for the immediate relief of pain on natural teeth, and that ceiling barely moves between tiers. The single article cap is what catches people out: £400 on Supreme is generous by market standards but still short of a camera body or a laptop, and gadget cover is a separate option that cannot be added to a long stay policy running beyond 120 days.

sections.heading: Where the activity list actually stops
sections.html:
Those 100-plus activities come with their limits attached, which is more useful than a marketing claim. Scuba diving is covered to 15 metres as standard, 30 metres with the Action option and 40 metres with Action Plus. Hiking and trekking reach 4,250 metres. Glacier walking is covered below 2,000 metres as standard and between 2,000 and 4,000 metres on Action. Canoeing, kayaking and white water rafting are grades 1 to 3 as standard, with grade 4 and above needing Action. Bungee jumping runs to three jumps. Sailing is covered within 60 miles of a safe haven, and small boating within the 12-mile limit on craft up to 10 metres.

Action Plus reaches further again, adding canyoning, heli-skiing and cat-skiing, non-racing horse riding, rugby, American football, hurling, competitive cycling other than BMX, and judo, karate, kendo and kick boxing. Winter sports run to 21 days a year on an annual multi-trip policy and up to 31 days on single trip and long stay cover, both for extra premium.

Some things sit outside the appetite altogether. Downhill and competitive mountain biking, horse racing, hunting on horseback, BMX and stunt cycling, mixed martial arts and any professional participation are not covered at any price. Nor, specifically, is scuba diving in Cyprus. Motorcycling can be arranged but drops the personal accident section. Anyone buying on the strength of the headline count should read the entry for their own sport rather than the total.

sections.heading: Going where the FCDO says not to
sections.html:
Voyager Plus follows the market on government advice: there is no cover for travel to an area the FCDO has advised against all, or all but essential, travel. Belarus, Cuba, Iran, North Korea, Russia, Syria and Ukraine are excluded outright under sanctions wording.

The unusual part is that Voyager sells the answer to its own exclusion. High Risk Voyager is a separate brand, underwritten by the same insurer, written for aid workers, missionaries, journalists, volunteers and contractors heading to Iraq, Nigeria, Libya, Afghanistan, Pakistan, Sri Lanka and similar. It adds political and natural disaster evacuation, hijack and mugging benefits and post-traumatic stress counselling to the usual medical and repatriation sections. Israel, Kuwait, Lebanon, Sudan, South Sudan, Syria, Ukraine, Venezuela and Yemen are assessed case by case rather than quoted online; India needs a referral within 10 kilometres of the Pakistan border and in Jammu and Kashmir; and Belarus, Russia, Crimea, Luhansk, Donetsk, Zaporizhzhia and Kherson stay excluded. Annual multi-trip cover on that brand stops once anyone on the policy reaches 70.

It carries its own exclusions worth knowing about: nothing where vaccination requirements were not met, nothing for armed forces on operational duty, nothing for a newly declared infectious disease once the World Health Organization designates a public health emergency of international concern, and no pregnancy or childbirth claim where the expected date of birth falls before or within eight weeks of travel. The insurer also reserves the right to require repatriation if an epidemic is declared at the destination.

sections.heading: Who is actually behind the policy
sections.html:
Voyager arranges; it does not carry the risk. Policies for UK, Channel Islands, Isle of Man and Gibraltar residents are underwritten by Starr International (Europe) Limited, firm reference 472977, regulated by the Prudential Regulation Authority and the Financial Conduct Authority. EEA residents get Starr Europe Insurance Limited, supervised in Malta. Starr’s insurance subsidiaries hold an A (Excellent) financial strength rating and an a+ long-term issuer credit rating from AM Best, most recently affirmed on 19 December 2023.

The arranging firm has changed hands. The company incorporated on 19 September 1996 as Voyager Insurance Services Limited was acquired by Caledon Group in July 2024 and renamed Caledon MGA Ltd on 19 June 2025, keeping Voyager as a trading style. Caledon Group was formed in 2023 by David Whitaker, Andrew Cross and Paul Davies, and also holds Somerville Group, the 75 per cent shareholder of record since April 2016. The firm reference number, 305814, has not changed and is verifiable on the FCA Register — but anyone searching that register for ‘Voyager’ will find the entry filed under Caledon.

The sale is non-advised. Voyager states plainly that it gives no personal recommendation, acts as agent of the insurer, and is paid a percentage of premium plus a bonus if the book hits profit targets; customers can ask what that commission is at any time. Complaints go first to the Managing Director on 01483 806 680 with a 20 working day target, then to the Financial Ombudsman Service on 0800 023 4567, and the firm is covered by the Financial Services Compensation Scheme.

sections.heading: What the claims data says about buying travel cover in 2026
sections.html:
Travel is one of the harder personal lines to claim on, and the regulator’s own figures show it. The FCA published its general insurance value measures for calendar year 2025 on 21 July 2026: travel products accepted between 83 and 86 per cent of claims, against 99 per cent for motor and 62 to 71 per cent for home combined. Claims complaints ran at 5 to 6 per cent of claims registered, high for a retail line. Claims costs rose to 44–48 per cent of premium from 31–37 per cent the year before, with payouts up 47 per cent against premiums up 12 per cent.

The Financial Ombudsman Service took 4,451 new travel insurance complaints in 2025/26 and upheld 36 per cent of those it decided, against an average of 30 per cent across all financial products; the figure for the first quarter of 2026/27 was 32 per cent. Declined claims are the single largest cause, and under-declared medical history is the most common reason a travel claim fails.

Set against that, the Association of British Insurers reported £472 million paid on more than 500,000 travel claims in 2024, published on 21 November 2025. Medical expenses took 34 per cent of the money — some £262 million — at an average of £1,528 a claim. That average is the number to hold next to Voyager’s excesses: on Standard, a £150 excess removes roughly a tenth of a typical medical payment before anything else is argued about. Pre-existing conditions have to go through Voyager Healthcheck, online or on 01483 806 666, and cover for anything undeclared simply is not there.

sections.heading: The costs and cut-offs to check before you buy
sections.html:
None of this is hidden, but several of these appear only in the terms of business rather than on the quote page. Buying online is free of administration charges. Buying or renewing by telephone costs £12. Changing a policy by telephone outside the 14 day cooling-off period costs £12, and cancelling outside that window costs £12 as well. The cooling-off period is 14 days, shortened if departure falls inside it and gone entirely once travel has begun. Cancel a single trip policy after that and the refund is 50 per cent; cancel an annual multi-trip policy and the refund slides from 100 per cent before it starts to 60 per cent within two months, 50 within three, 40 within four, 30 within five, 25 within six and nothing thereafter.

The age and duration ceilings do a lot of the underwriting. Single trip cover has no upper age limit, but the trip caps at 62 days, dropping to 31 days for travellers over 74 and 31 days to every destination once anyone is 85 or over. Long stay cover stops at 69 at departure and runs to 24 months for under-50s and 18 months for those aged 51 to 60, with up to five home visits of two weeks each allowed. Annual multi-trip is available up to 79 at inception, with 45 days per trip as standard and 62 days available to under-70s for extra premium.

Covid-19 cover is narrower than the length of the wording suggests. It reaches only cancellation under section 1.2, emergency medical expenses, hospital stay benefit and the cruise rejoin cover, so pandemic disruption and curtailment largely sit outside the policy. There is also a broadly drawn excessive alcohol exclusion — defined as drinking enough to notably impair faculties or judgement — which is a common ground for declining a claim after an accident abroad.

pros: Over 100 sports and activities included as standard, each published with its own depth, altitude or grade limit rather than a vague exclusion
Emergency medical expenses of £10 million on the Prime and Supreme tiers, with the Supreme excess at £50
No upper age limit on single trip cover, and long stay policies running to 24 months for under-50s
High Risk Voyager gives a route to cover for FCDO-advised destinations that most insurers refuse outright
Underwritten by Starr International (Europe) Limited, rated A (Excellent) by AM Best
No administration fee on anything bought, amended or cancelled online
cons: The Standard tier is thin for the price of a holiday: a £1,000 cancellation limit will not cover many package trips, and its £150 excess removes about a tenth of the £1,528 average travel medical claim
The sale is non-advised, so choosing the wrong tier or missing an activity limit is entirely the buyer’s problem, and Voyager is paid a share of premium plus a profit bonus by the insurer
A £12 fee applies to buying, renewing, amending or cancelling by telephone, which falls hardest on customers who would rather not transact online
Long stay cover cuts off at 69 and annual multi-trip at 79, so older travellers making long trips are pushed onto single trip policies capped at 31 days once past 74
Scuba diving is only 15 metres as standard and is not covered at all in Cyprus, while downhill mountain biking, MMA and any professional participation are uninsurable at any price
Covid-19 cover is limited to four named sections, and the trading name no longer matches the legal entity, so the FCA Register entry appears under Caledon MGA Ltd rather than Voyager
verdict: Voyager Plus is a specialist product sold at retail, and it suits people whose trips do not fit a supermarket policy: trekkers at altitude, divers, long stay travellers and anyone whose destination carries FCDO advice. The published activity limits and the £10 million medical ceiling on the upper tiers are genuinely strong, and the £50 excess on Supreme is among the lowest in the market. Take the Standard tier only for a cheap trip you could afford to lose, because a £1,000 cancellation cap and a £150 excess do not stretch far. Buy online rather than by phone, put every medical condition through Healthcheck before you travel, and read the entry for your own activity rather than trusting the headline count.

faqs.q: Who underwrites Voyager travel insurance?
faqs.a: Starr International (Europe) Limited, firm reference 472977, underwrites policies for residents of the UK, Channel Islands, Isle of Man and Gibraltar, regulated by the Prudential Regulation Authority and the Financial Conduct Authority. EEA residents are covered by Starr Europe Insurance Limited, supervised in Malta. Starr’s insurance subsidiaries carry an A (Excellent) financial strength rating from AM Best, affirmed on 19 December 2023.

faqs.q: Is Voyager Insurance Services FCA authorised?
faqs.a: Yes. The arranging firm holds firm reference number 305814 and company number 3251842. The legal entity was renamed Caledon MGA Ltd on 19 June 2025, after Caledon Group acquired the business in July 2024, with Voyager kept on as a trading style — so the FCA Register entry appears under the Caledon name.

faqs.q: What excess does Voyager charge?
faqs.a: £150 per claim on Standard, £100 on Enhanced, £75 on Prime and £50 on Supreme. It applies per person per section claimed, so a couple claiming for medical costs and lost baggage on the same trip will meet it more than once.

faqs.q: Does Voyager cover travel against FCDO advice?
faqs.a: Not under the mainstream Voyager Plus policy, which excludes any area where the FCDO advises against all or all but essential travel. High Risk Voyager is a separate purchase, underwritten by the same insurer, covering destinations such as Iraq, Nigeria, Libya, Afghanistan and Pakistan. Israel, Kuwait, Lebanon, Sudan, South Sudan, Syria, Ukraine, Venezuela and Yemen are quoted case by case, and Belarus, Russia and the occupied Ukrainian oblasts stay excluded.

faqs.q: How deep can I scuba dive on a Voyager policy?
faqs.a: Fifteen metres as standard, 30 metres with the Action option and 40 metres with Action Plus, always on an amateur basis and within your certification or with a qualified instructor. Diving in Cyprus is not covered on any level.

faqs.q: How do I complain about Voyager?
faqs.a: Complaints go first to the Managing Director on 01483 806 680, with a stated target of 20 working days for a final response. If you are unhappy with the outcome you can take the case to the Financial Ombudsman Service on 0800 023 4567. The service upheld 36 per cent of the 4,451 travel insurance complaints it handled in 2025/26.

title: Wicked Quotes Motorbike Insurance Review
meta_title: Wicked Quotes Bike Insurance: Aviva and AXA Behind It
meta_description: Wicked Quotes is the retail arm of Novitas, an underwriting agency using Aviva and AXA paper. Nine-question quotes, £20m cover and the fees to know first.
intro:
Wicked Quotes sells one thing, motorcycle insurance, and it has sold it under that name for more than fifteen years from an office at 28 Station Close in Potters Bar. The quote form is about as short as they come: nine questions, no name and no phone number required, and a rough price on screen before you have given anything away. Sales lines are open 9am to 5pm Monday to Friday and 9am to 1pm on Saturday on 0344 8800 962, and the staff answering them are described as riders themselves.

The firm behind the brand has rather more history than the name suggests. Wicked Quotes is a trading name of Novitas Underwriting Agency Limited, company 03106533, incorporated on 26 September 1995 and trading since 1996. Novitas is an underwriting agency rather than a high-street broker: it holds authority to price and arrange cover on insurers' behalf, and describes itself as acting for “a number of market leading UK insurers including Aviva and Markerstudy”. Its own published product assessment maps its motorcycle schemes to Aviva and AXA. For a rider, that is the part worth knowing — the paper behind the policy comes from large, familiar names.

Novitas also supplies more than 150 brokers and intermediaries across the UK, so the same underwriting may well sit behind quotes you have been given elsewhere. Cover runs from third party only through third party fire and theft to comprehensive, with separate routes for modified bikes, high-value machines, multi-bike households and couriers, food delivery excepted. The firm is authorised and regulated by the Financial Conduct Authority under firm reference 307931, which anyone can check on the FCA Register.
